# Reimplementation of structlog setup with equivalent functionality but different structure

import os
import sys
import logging
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from typing import Dict, Any, Optional
import pytz
import sanic
import structlog
from pythonjsonlogger import jsonlogger
from structlog.contextvars import merge_contextvars

STRUCTLOG_MARKER = "is_structlog"


def configure_logging(
    *,
    verbosity: Optional[str] = None,
    format_style: Optional[str] = None,
):
    """Set up structured logging with configurable level and output style.
    
    Args:
        verbosity (str): Logging severity threshold; defaults to LOG_LEVEL env var or "INFO"
        format_style (str): Output format - either "json" or "pretty"; defaults to 
            environment variable or auto-detects based on terminal attachment
    """
    # Normalize environment variables to lowercase keys
    env_vars = {k.lower(): v for k, v in os.environ.items()}
    
    # Determine log level
    if verbosity is None:
        verbosity = env_vars.get("log_level", "INFO")
    
    # Determine output format style
    if format_style is None:
        terminal_check = sys.stdout.isatty()
        format_style = env_vars.get("log_style", "pretty" if terminal_check else "json")
    
    # Set up shared handler for all loggers
    stream_handler = logging.StreamHandler()
    
    # Attach handler to Sanic loggers
    sanic.log.access_logger.addHandler(stream_handler)
    sanic.log.error_logger.addHandler(stream_handler)
    sanic.log.logger.addHandler(stream_handler)
    
    # Attach to root logger if no handlers exist yet
    if not logging.root.handlers:
        logging.root.addHandler(stream_handler)
    
    # Configure structlog processors based on output style
    if format_style == "pretty":
        processor_chain = [
            merge_contextvars,
            structlog.stdlib.add_logger_name,
            structlog.stdlib.add_log_level,
            structlog.stdlib.PositionalArgumentsFormatter(),
            structlog.processors.StackInfoRenderer(),
            structlog.processors.format_exc_info,
            structlog.processors.UnicodeDecoder(),
            structlog.processors.ExceptionPrettyPrinter(),
            structlog.dev.ConsoleRenderer(),
        ]
    elif format_style == "json":
        processor_chain = [
            merge_contextvars,
            structlog.stdlib.filter_by_level,
            structlog.stdlib.add_logger_name,
            structlog.stdlib.add_log_level,
            structlog.stdlib.PositionalArgumentsFormatter(),
            structlog.processors.StackInfoRenderer(),
            structlog.processors.format_exc_info,
            structlog.processors.UnicodeDecoder(),
            structlog.stdlib.render_to_log_kwargs,
            _mark_structlog_event,
        ]
        
        # Apply custom JSON formatter to all handlers
        json_formatter = StructuredJsonFormatter()
        stream_handler.setFormatter(json_formatter)
        
        for handler in logging.root.handlers:
            handler.setFormatter(json_formatter)
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"Unsupported LOG_STYLE='{format_style}'")
    
    # Final structlog configuration
    structlog.configure(
        processors=processor_chain,
        context_class=dict,
        logger_factory=structlog.stdlib.LoggerFactory(),
        wrapper_class=structlog.stdlib.BoundLogger,
        cache_logger_on_first_use=True,
    )
    
    # Set global logging level
    logging.root.setLevel(verbosity)


def _mark_structlog_event(logger, name, event_dict):
    """Add marker to indicate this event originated from structlog"""
    event_dict["extra"][STRUCTLOG_MARKER] = True
    return event_dict


def _ensure_field(record: Dict[str, Any], field_name: str, value: Any):
    """Add a field to the record only if it doesn't already exist"""
    if field_name not in record:
        record[field_name] = value


class StructuredJsonFormatter(jsonlogger.JsonFormatter):
    """Custom JSON formatter that handles both structlog and standard log entries"""
    
    def add_fields(self, log_record, record, message_dict):
        super().add_fields(log_record, record, message_dict)
        
        # Remove structlog marker if present
        if log_record.get(STRUCTLOG_MARKER) is True:
            del log_record[STRUCTLOG_MARKER]
        else:
            # Add context variables for non-structlog events
            context_data = merge_contextvars(None, None, {})
            log_record.update(context_data)
        
        # Add timestamp information
        utc_time = datetime.fromtimestamp(record.created, tz=timezone.utc)
        
        _ensure_field(log_record, "timestamp", utc_time.isoformat())
        
        _ensure_field(log_record, "timestamps", {
            "epoch": record.created,
            "utc": utc_time.isoformat(),
            "montreal": utc_time.astimezone(
                pytz.timezone("America/Montreal")
            ).isoformat(),
        })
        
        # Add additional metadata fields
        _ensure_field(log_record, "logger", record.name)
        _ensure_field(log_record, "level", record.levelname.lower())
        _ensure_field(log_record, "lineno", record.lineno)
        _ensure_field(log_record, "pathname", record.pathname)
        _ensure_field(log_record, "threadName", record.threadName)
        _ensure_field(log_record, "processName", record.processName)

# Type III Clone: Modified BLAST API wrapper with equivalent functionality import re import time import logging import requests from Bio.Blast import NCBIWWW from cblaster import helpers from cblaster.classes import Hit LOG = logging.getLogger(__name__) NCBI_BLAST_ENDPOINT = "https://blast.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/Blast.cgi" def initiate( sequences=None, query_file=None, query_ids=None, target_db="nr", blast_type="blastp", mega_mode=False, filter_option="F", e_value=10, nucleotide_reward=None, nucleotide_penalty=None, gap_parameters="11 1", scoring_matrix="BLOSUM62", max_hits=5000, min_word_score=11, word_length=6, comp_stats=2, filter_entrez=None, ): """Initiate a remote BLAST search via NCBI's web API. This function replaces 'start' with altered parameter names and logic flow while maintaining identical behavior. """ if not sequences: sequences = helpers.get_sequences( query_file=query_file, query_ids=query_ids ) query_data = helpers.sequences_to_fasta(sequences) config = { "CMD": "PUT", "DATABASE": target_db, "PROGRAM": blast_type, "FILTER": filter_option, "EXPECT": e_value, "GAPCOSTS": gap_parameters, "MATRIX": scoring_matrix, "HITLIST_SIZE": max_hits, "ALIGNMENTS": max_hits, "DESCRIPTIONS": max_hits, "WORD_SIZE": word_length, "COMPOSITION_BASED_STATISTICS": comp_stats, } if filter_entrez: config["ENTREZ_QUERY"] = filter_entrez if blast_type == "blastn": if mega_mode: config["MEGABLAST"] = "on" if nucleotide_reward is not None: config["NUCL_REWARD"] = nucleotide_reward if nucleotide_penalty is not None: config["NUCL_PENALTY"] = nucleotide_penalty else: config["THRESHOLD"] = min_word_score response = requests.post(NCBI_BLAST_ENDPOINT, files={"QUERY": query_data}, params=config) LOG.debug("Search configuration: %s", config) LOG.debug("Search request URL: %s", response.url) rid_match, rtoe_match = re.findall(r"(?:RID|RTOE) = (.+?)[\n\s]", response.text) return rid_match, int(rtoe_match) def status_check(rid): """Check completion status of a BLAST search using Request Identifier (RID). This function replaces 'check' with modified implementation and variable names. """ parameters = {"CMD": "Get", "RID": rid, "FORMAT_OBJECT": "SearchInfo"} response = requests.get(NCBI_BLAST_ENDPOINT, params=parameters) LOG.debug(response.url) info = re.findall(r"(?:Status|ThereAreHits)=(.+?)[\n\s]", response.text) if len(info) == 1: current_status = info[0] if current_status in ("UNKNOWN", "FAILED"): raise ValueError(f"BLAST search {rid} failed (status={current_status})") if current_status == "WAITING": return False if info == ["READY", "yes"]: return True raise ValueError("Search completed, but found no hits") def fetch_results(rid, max_hits=5000): """Retrieve BLAST results for a given Request Identifier (RID). This function replaces 'retrieve' with different control flow and variable naming. """ params = { "CMD": "Get", "RID": rid, "FORMAT_TYPE": "Tabular", "FORMAT_OBJECT": "Alignment", "HITLIST_SIZE": max_hits, "ALIGNMENTS": max_hits, "DESCRIPTIONS": max_hits, "NCBI_GI": "F", } LOG.debug(params) response = requests.get(NCBI_BLAST_ENDPOINT, params=params) LOG.debug(response.url) # Extract content between 
 tags and clean up
    raw_content = re.search("
(.+?)
", response.text, re.DOTALL).group(1)
    return [
        line for line in raw_content.split("\n") 
        if line and not line.startswith("#")
    ]

def monitor(rid, interval=60, retry_limit=-1):
    """Poll BLAST API at regular intervals until results are available.
    
    This function replaces 'poll' with adjusted timing logic and variable names.
    """
    if interval < 60:
        raise ValueError("Interval must be at least 60 seconds")
        
    attempts, last_time = 0, 0
    
    while True:
        now = time.time()
        delay = last_time - now + interval
        
        if delay > 0:
            time.sleep(delay)
            last_time = now + delay
        else:
            last_time = now
            
        LOG.info("Verifying search progress...")
        if status_check(rid):
            LOG.info("Search completed successfully!")
            return
            
        if retry_limit > 0 and attempts == retry_limit:
            raise ValueError(f"Exceeded maximum retry attempts ({retry_limit})")
            
        attempts += 1

def process_results(
    data,
    sequences=None,
    query_file=None,
    query_ids=None,
    evalue_threshold=0.01,
    identity_threshold=30,
    coverage_threshold=50,
):
    """Process Tabular BLAST results with filtering criteria.
    
    This function replaces 'parse' with modified validation and variable naming.
    """
    if not sequences:
        sequences = helpers.get_sequences(query_file, query_ids)
        
    significant_hits = []
    
    for record in data:
        qid, sid, pident, *_, qstart, qend, _, _, evalue, score, _ = record.split("\t")
        
        # Calculate query coverage manually
        alignment_length = int(qend) - int(qstart) + 1
        coverage_pct = (alignment_length / len(sequences[qid])) * 100
        
        hit = Hit(
            query=qid,
            subject=sid,
            identity=pident,
            coverage=coverage_pct,
            evalue=evalue,
            bitscore=score,
        )
        
        if (
            float(hit.identity) > identity_threshold and
            float(hit.coverage) > coverage_threshold and
            hit.evalue < evalue_threshold
        ):
            significant_hits.append(hit)
            
    if not significant_hits:
        raise ValueError("No hits met the specified thresholds")
        
    return significant_hits

def execute(
    rid=None,
    sequences=None,
    query_file=None,
    query_ids=None,
    identity_cutoff=0.3,
    coverage_cutoff=0.5,
    evalue_limit=0.01,
    output_file=None,
    max_targets=500,
    **kwargs,
):
    """Perform complete BLAST workflow: launch, wait, retrieve, and parse.
    
    This function replaces 'search' with modified defaults and internal logic.
    """
    if not rid:
        LOG.info("Starting new BLAST search")
        rid, eta = initiate(
            sequences=sequences,
            query_file=query_file,
            query_ids=query_ids,
            max_hits=max_targets,
            **kwargs
        )
        LOG.info("Request Identifier (RID): %s", rid)
        LOG.info("Estimated execution time: %ss", eta)
        time.sleep(eta)
        
    LOG.info("Monitoring search status")
    monitor(rid)
    
    LOG.info("Fetching results for search %s", rid)
    raw_output = fetch_results(rid, max_hits=max_targets)
    
    if output_file:
        LOG.info("Saving BLAST results to %s", output_file)
        with open(output_file, "w") as f:
            f.write("\n".join(raw_output))
            
    LOG.info("Processing BLAST results...")
    filtered_hits = process_results(
        raw_output,
        sequences=sequences,
        query_file=query_file,
        query_ids=query_ids,
        evalue_threshold=evalue_limit,
        identity_threshold=identity_cutoff * 100,
        coverage_threshold=coverage_cutoff * 100,
    )
    
    return rid, filtered_hits

@numba.njit(nogil=True)
def construct_skip_gram_tuples(
    token_list,
    per_token_windows,
    weight_func,
    weight_params,
    backward=False,
):
    """Generate skip-gram representations for a single token sequence.
    
    Creates weighted co-occurrence relationships between tokens within 
    dynamically-sized windows. Each relationship is represented as a 
    (head_token, tail_token, weight) tuple.
    
    Parameters
    ----------
    token_list: sequence of int
        The token indices to process
    per_token_windows: array-like
        Window sizes indexed by token type
    weight_func: jitted function
        Computes weights based on distance from center token
    weight_params: tuple
        Additional parameters for weight computation
    backward: bool
        If True, look backwards; otherwise look forwards
        
    Returns
    -------
    list of tuples
        Skip-gram triplets in (head, tail, weight) format
    """
    result = [(0.0, 0.0, 0.0)]
    for pos, center_token in enumerate(token_list):
        # Get context window around current position
        context = window_at_index(token_list, per_token_windows[center_token], pos, backward)
        
        # Compute weights for each context token
        weights = weight_func(context, *weight_params)
        
        # Add all (center_token, context_token, weight) combinations
        for idx in range(len(context)):
            result.append((float(center_token), float(context[idx]), weights[idx]))
    
    return sum_coo_entries(result)


def generate_skip_gram_features(
    sequences,
    window_configurations,
    weighting_scheme,
    weighting_options,
):
    """Construct sparse matrix representation of skip-grams across multiple sequences.
    
    Parameters
    ----------
    sequences: collection of token sequences
    window_configurations: per-token window size specifications
    weighting_scheme: callable or string identifier for kernel function
    weighting_options: additional parameters for weighting
    
    Returns
    -------
    row_indices: array of int
        Row positions for sparse matrix entries
    col_indices: array of int
        Column positions for sparse matrix entries
    values: array of float
        Skip-gram weights at corresponding positions
    """
    rows = []
    cols = []
    vals = []
    
    vocab_size = len(window_configurations) - 1
    
    for seq_id, seq in enumerate(sequences):
        # Process each sequence into skip-grams
        grams = construct_skip_gram_tuples(
            seq,
            window_configurations,
            weighting_scheme,
            weighting_options,
        )
        
        # Map skip-grams to matrix coordinates
        for gram in grams:
            rows.append(seq_id)
            head_idx = int(gram[0])
            tail_idx = int(gram[1])
            # Create unique column index for ordered pair
            cols.append(head_idx * vocab_size + tail_idx)
            vals.append(gram[2])
    
    return np.array(rows), np.array(cols), np.array(vals)


@numba.njit(nogil=True)
def aggregate_skip_grams(
    batch_sequences,
    window_specifications,
    kernel_function,
    kernel_parameters,
    direction_backward=False,
):
    """Combine skip-gram data from multiple sequences into unified representation.
    
    Parameters
    ----------
    batch_sequences: list of token sequences
    window_specifications: per-token window configurations
    kernel_function: weighting function
    kernel_parameters: arguments for weighting function
    direction_backward: process context before or after current token
    
    Returns
    -------
    aggregated_grams: array of shape (n_grams, 3)
        Combined skip-gram data from all sequences
    """
    combined = [(0.0, 0.0, 0.0)]
    
    for sequence in batch_sequences:
        # Accumulate skip-grams from each sequence
        combined.extend(
            construct_skip_gram_tuples(
                sequence,
                window_specifications,
                kernel_function,
                kernel_parameters,
                direction_backward,
            )
        )
    
    return np.array(sum_coo_entries(combined))


class SkipgramVectorizer(BaseEstimator, TransformerMixin):
    """Vectorize token sequences using kernel-weighted skip-gram co-occurrences.
    
    Processes either single sequences or batches of sequences, creating a 
    sparse matrix where each column represents an ordered token pair and 
    each entry counts weighted co-occurrences.
    
    Parameters
    ----------
    token_dictionary : dict or None
        Predefined mapping from tokens to indices
    max_unique_tokens : int or None
        Maximum vocabulary size (top frequent tokens kept)
    min_occurrences : int or None
        Minimum occurrence threshold for tokens
    max_occurrences : int or None
        Maximum occurrence threshold for tokens
    min_frequency : float or None
        Minimum frequency threshold for tokens
    max_frequency : float or None
        Maximum frequency threshold for tokens
    min_document_occurrences : int or None
        Minimum document frequency threshold
    max_document_occurrences : int or None
        Maximum document frequency threshold
    min_document_frequency : float or None
        Minimum document frequency ratio
    max_document_frequency : float or None
        Maximum document frequency ratio
    max_unique_tokens : int or None
        Upper bound on vocabulary size
    ignored_tokens : set or None
        Tokens to exclude from processing
    excluded_token_regex : str or None
        Regex pattern for excluding tokens
    window_function : callable or str
        Function to determine window sizes per token
    kernel_function : callable or str
        Function to compute weights within windows
    window_args : dict
        Arguments for window function
    kernel_args : dict
        Arguments for kernel function
    window_radius : int
        Base parameter for window sizing
    validate_data : bool
        Whether to validate input data types
    mask_string : str or None
        Special token to use for masking
    nullify_mask : bool
        Whether to ignore masked tokens
    """
    
    def __init__(
        self,
        token_dictionary=None,
        min_occurrences=None,
        max_occurrences=None,
        min_frequency=None,
        max_frequency=None,
        min_document_occurrences=None,
        max_document_occurrences=None,
        min_document_frequency=None,
        max_document_frequency=None,
        max_unique_tokens=None,
        ignored_tokens=None,
        excluded_token_regex=None,
        window_function="fixed",
        kernel_function="flat",
        window_args=dict(),
        kernel_args=dict(),
        window_radius=5,
        validate_data=True,
        mask_string=None,
        nullify_mask=False,
    ):
        # Store configuration parameters
        self.token_dictionary = token_dictionary
        self.max_unique_tokens = max_unique_tokens
        self.min_occurrences = min_occurrences
        self.min_frequency = min_frequency
        self.max_occurrences = max_occurrences
        self.max_frequency = max_frequency
        self.min_document_occurrences = min_document_occurrences
        self.min_document_frequency = min_document_frequency
        self.max_document_occurrences = max_document_occurrences
        self.max_document_frequency = max_document_frequency
        self.ignored_tokens = ignored_tokens
        self.excluded_token_regex = excluded_token_regex
        self.window_function = window_function
        self.kernel_function = kernel_function
        self.window_args = window_args
        self.kernel_args = kernel_args
        self.window_radius = window_radius
        self.validate_data = validate_data
        self.mask_string = mask_string
        self.nullify_mask = nullify_mask

    def fit(self, X, y=None, **fit_params):
        # Validate input if requested
        if self.validate_data:
            validate_homogeneous_token_types(X)
        
        # Flatten input sequences
        flat_sequence = flatten(X)
        
        # Preprocess and build vocabulary
        (token_sequences,
         self._token_dictionary_,
         self._inverse_token_dictionary_,
         self._token_frequencies_) = preprocess_token_sequences(
            X,
            flat_sequence,
            token_dictionary=self.token_dictionary,
            max_unique_tokens=self.max_unique_tokens,
            min_occurrences=self.min_occurrences,
            max_occurrences=self.max_occurrences,
            min_frequency=self.min_frequency,
            max_frequency=self.max_frequency,
            min_document_occurrences=self.min_document_occurrences,
            max_document_occurrences=self.max_document_occurrences,
            min_document_frequency=self.min_document_frequency,
            max_document_frequency=self.max_document_frequency,
            ignored_tokens=self.ignored_tokens,
            excluded_token_regex=self.excluded_token_regex,
        )
        
        # Resolve kernel function
        if callable(self.kernel_function):
            self._kernel_function = self.kernel_function
        elif self.kernel_function in _KERNEL_FUNCTIONS:
            self._kernel_function = _KERNEL_FUNCTIONS[self.kernel_function]
        else:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Invalid kernel_function. Must be callable or one of {_KERNEL_FUNCTIONS.keys()}"
            )
        
        # Resolve window function
        if callable(self.window_function):
            self._window_function = self.window_function
        elif self.window_function in _WINDOW_FUNCTIONS:
            self._window_function = _WINDOW_FUNCTIONS[self.window_function]
        else:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Invalid window_function. Must be callable or one of {_WINDOW_FUNCTIONS.keys()}"
            )
        
        # Handle masking
        if self.nullify_mask:
            if self.mask_string is None:
                raise ValueError("Cannot suppress mask with mask_string = None")
            mask_index = len(self._token_frequencies_)
        else:
            mask_index = None
        
        # Prepare kernel arguments
        self._kernel_args = {
            "mask_index": mask_index,
            "normalize": False,
            "offset": 0
        }
        self._kernel_args.update(self.kernel_args)
        self._kernel_args = tuple(self._kernel_args.values())
        
        # Generate window sizes per token
        self._window_sizes = self._window_function(
            self.window_radius,
            self._token_frequencies_,
            mask_index,
            *self.window_args.values()
        )
        
        # Build skip-gram matrix
        row, col, data = generate_skip_gram_features(
            token_sequences,
            self._window_sizes,
            self._kernel_function,
            self._kernel_args,
        )
        
        # Construct sparse matrix
        base_matrix = scipy.sparse.coo_matrix((data, (row, col)))
        
        # Determine active columns
        column_sums = np.array(base_matrix.sum(axis=0))[0]
        self._column_is_kept = column_sums > 0
        self._kept_columns = np.where(self._column_is_kept)[0]
        
        # Build column label mappings
        self.column_label_dictionary_ = {}
        for i, col_idx in enumerate(self._kept_columns):
            raw_val = col_idx
            first_token = self._inverse_token_dictionary_[
                raw_val // len(self._token_dictionary_)
            ]
            second_token = self._inverse_token_dictionary_[
                raw_val % len(self._token_dictionary_)
            ]
            self.column_label_dictionary_[(first_token, second_token)] = i
        
        self.column_index_dictionary_ = {
            val: key for key, val in self.column_label_dictionary_.items()
        }
        
        # Store processed training matrix
        self._train_matrix = base_matrix.tocsc()[:, self._column_is_kept].tocsr()
        self._train_matrix.eliminate_zeros()
        self.metric_ = distances.sparse_hellinger
        
        return self

    def fit_transform(self, X, y=None, **fit_params):
        self.fit(X, y, **fit_params)
        return self._train_matrix

    def transform(self, X):
        check_is_fitted(
            self,
            ["_token_dictionary_", "_column_is_kept"],
        )
        
        # Process new sequences
        flat_sequence = flatten(X)
        (token_sequences, _, _, _) = preprocess_token_sequences(
            X,
            flat_sequence,
            self._token_dictionary_,
        )
        
        # Generate skip-gram features
        n_vocab = len(self._token_dictionary_)
        row, col, data = generate_skip_gram_features(
            token_sequences,
            self._window_sizes,
            self._kernel_function,
            self._kernel_args,
        )
        
        # Transform to appropriate sparse format
        base_matrix = scipy.sparse.coo_matrix((data, (row, col)))
        result = base_matrix.tocsc()[:, self._column_is_kept].tocsr()
        
        return result

import asyncio
import logging
from typing import Dict, Tuple, Union, cast
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from opentrons.util.helpers import utc_now
from opentrons.config import IS_ROBOT
from robot_server.system import errors
from robot_server.service.errors import CommonErrorDef

_logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

def _parse_status_output(status_text: str) -> Dict[str, Union[str, bool]]:
    """Parse the output of timedatectl show into a dictionary."""
    parsed_data = {}
    for line in status_text.strip().splitlines():
        if not line:
            continue
        try:
            key, value = line.split("=", 1)
            # Convert string boolean representations
            if value.lower() == "yes":
                parsed_data[key] = True
            elif value.lower() == "no":
                parsed_data[key] = False
            else:
                parsed_data[key] = value
        except ValueError as exc:
            _logger.warning(f"Failed to parse timedatectl line: '{line}' - {exc}")
    return cast(Dict[str, Union[str, bool]], parsed_data)

async def _fetch_time_status() -> Dict[str, Union[str, bool]]:
    """Retrieve current time synchronization status from the system."""
    process = await asyncio.create_subprocess_shell(
        "timedatectl show",
        stdout=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
        stderr=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
        loop=asyncio.get_event_loop(),
    )
    stdout_data, stderr_data = await process.communicate()
    return _parse_status_output(stdout_data.decode())

async def _execute_time_update(time_string: str) -> Tuple[str, str]:
    """Execute command to update system time and capture output/error."""
    process = await asyncio.create_subprocess_shell(
        f'date --utc --set "{time_string}"',
        stdout=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
        stderr=asyncio.subprocess.PIPE,
        loop=asyncio.get_event_loop(),
    )
    stdout_bytes, stderr_bytes = await process.communicate()
    return stdout_bytes.decode(), stderr_bytes.decode()

async def retrieve_current_time() -> datetime:
    """Fetch the current system time in UTC."""
    return utc_now()

async def adjust_system_time(target_time: datetime) -> datetime:
    """Update the system clock to the specified time.
    
    This function prevents setting time when NTP or hardware RTC is active.
    
    Args:
        target_time: The desired UTC datetime to set.
        
    Returns:
        The confirmed system time after attempting adjustment.
        
    Raises:
        SystemSetTimeException: If time setting fails due to execution error.
        SystemTimeAlreadySynchronized: If time is managed by NTP/RTC.
    """
    if not IS_ROBOT:
        raise errors.SystemSetTimeException(
            msg="Operation not available on development server.",
            definition=CommonErrorDef.NOT_IMPLEMENTED,
        )

    sys_status = await _fetch_time_status()
    
    # Check if time synchronization mechanisms are active
    rtc_active = sys_status.get("LocalRTC", False)
    ntp_active = sys_status.get("NTPSynchronized", False)
    
    if rtc_active or ntp_active:
        raise errors.SystemTimeAlreadySynchronized(
            "System time cannot be manually adjusted while synchronized"
        )

    # Convert and format target time
    utc_target = target_time.astimezone(timezone.utc)
    formatted_time = utc_target.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")
    
    _logger.info(f"Updating system time to {formatted_time} UTC")
    
    _, error_msg = await _execute_time_update(formatted_time)
    
    if error_msg:
        raise errors.SystemSetTimeException(error_msg)
    
    return utc_now()

from __future__ import absolute_import

class ExternalDataInfo(object):
    def __init__(self, tensor):  # type: (TensorProto) -> None
        self.location = ''
        self.offset = None
        self.length = None
        self.checksum = None
        self.basepath = ''
        
        # Process external_data entries using list comprehension instead of setattr loop
        data_map = {entry.key: entry.value for entry in tensor.external_data}
        self.location = data_map.get('location', '')
        self.offset = int(data_map['offset']) if 'offset' in data_map else None
        self.length = int(data_map['length']) if 'length' in data_map else None
        
def load_external_data_for_tensor(tensor, base_dir):  # type: (TensorProto, Text) -> None
    """
    Load data from an external file for tensor.
    @params
    tensor: a TensorProto object.
    base_dir: directory that contains the external data.
    """
    if tensor.raw_data:  # already loaded
        return
        
    info = ExternalDataInfo(tensor)
    safe_path = _clean_path(info.location)
    full_path = os.path.join(base_dir, safe_path)
    
    try:
        with open(full_path, 'rb') as data_file:
            if info.offset is not None:
                data_file.seek(info.offset)
                
            read_size = info.length if info.length is not None else -1
            tensor.raw_data = data_file.read(read_size) if read_size != -1 else data_file.read()
    except IOError:
        raise RuntimeError(f"Failed to read external data file: {full_path}")

def load_external_data_for_model(model, base_dir):  # type: (ModelProto, Text) -> None
    """
    Loads external tensors into model
    @params
    model: ModelProto to load external data to
    base_dir: directory that contains external data
    """
    for tensor in _collect_all_tensors(model):
        if uses_external_data(tensor):
            load_external_data_for_tensor(tensor, base_dir)
            tensor.data_location = TensorProto.DEFAULT
            del tensor.external_data[:]

def set_external_data(tensor,  # type: TensorProto
                      location,  # type: Text
                      offset=None,  # type: Optional[int]
                      length=None,  # type: Optional[int]
                      checksum=None,  # type: Optional[Text]
                      basepath=None  # type: Optional[Text]
                      ):  # type: (...) -> None
    if not tensor.raw_data:
        raise ValueError("Tensor " + tensor.name + " does not have raw_data field. Cannot set external data for this tensor.")
        
    # Clear existing external_data entries
    tensor.external_data[:] = []
    tensor.data_location = TensorProto.EXTERNAL
    
    # Build external data dictionary and add non-None values
    data_dict = {
        'location': location,
        'offset': str(int(offset)) if offset is not None else None,
        'length': str(int(length)) if length is not None else None,
        'checksum': checksum,
        'basepath': basepath
    }
    
    for key, value in data_dict.items():
        if value is not None:
            entry = tensor.external_data.add()
            entry.key = key
            entry.value = value

def convert_model_to_external_data(model, all_tensors_to_one_file=True, location=None, size_threshold=1024, convert_attribute=False):
    # type: (ModelProto, bool, Optional[Text], int, bool) -> None
    """
    Call to set all tensors with raw data as external data. This call should preceed 'save_model'.
    'save_model' saves all the tensors data as external data after calling this function.
    @params
    model: ModelProto to be converted.
    all_tensors_to_one_file: If true, save all tensors to one external file specified by location.
                             If false, save each tensor to a file named with the tensor name.
    location: specify the external file that all tensors to save to.
              If not specified, will use the model name.
    size_threshold: Threshold for size of data. Only when tensor's data is >= the size_threshold
    it will be converted to external data. To convert every tensor with raw data to external data set size_threshold=0.
    convert_attribute: If true, convert all tensors to external data
                       If false, convert only non-attribute tensors to external data
    """
    tensors = _get_initializer_tensors(model)
    if convert_attribute:
        tensors = _collect_all_tensors(model)
        
    if all_tensors_to_one_file:
        file_name = Text(uuid.uuid1())
        if location:
            file_name = location
            
        for tensor in tensors:
            if tensor.raw_data and sys.getsizeof(tensor.raw_data) >= size_threshold:
                set_external_data(tensor, file_name)
    else:
        for tensor in tensors:
            if tensor.raw_data and sys.getsizeof(tensor.raw_data) >= size_threshold:
                tensor_location = tensor.name
                if not _is_valid_filename(tensor_location):
                    tensor_location = Text(uuid.uuid1())
                set_external_data(tensor, tensor_location)

def convert_model_from_external_data(model):  # type: (ModelProto) -> None
    """
    Call to set all tensors which use external data as embedded data. save_model saves all the tensors data as embedded data after calling this function.
    @params
    model: ModelProto to be converted.
    """
    for tensor in _collect_all_tensors(model):
        if uses_external_data(tensor):
            if not tensor.raw_data:
                raise ValueError("raw_data field doesn't exist.")
            tensor.external_data[:] = []
            tensor.data_location = TensorProto.DEFAULT

def save_external_data(tensor, base_path):  # type: (TensorProto, Text) -> None
    """
    Write tensor data to an external file according to information in the `external_data` field.
    @params
    tensor: Tensor object to be serialized
    base_path: System path of a folder where tensor data is to be stored
    """
    info = ExternalDataInfo(tensor)
    full_path = os.path.join(base_path, info.location)
    
    if not tensor.raw_data:
        raise ValueError("raw_data field doesn't exist.")
        
    # Ensure file exists
    if not os.path.exists(full_path):
        with open(full_path, 'ab'):
            pass
            
    # Open file for random access writing
    with open(full_path, 'r+b') as data_file:
        data_file.seek(0, 2)  # Seek to end
        current_pos = data_file.tell()
        
        # Handle offset padding if needed
        if info.offset is not None and info.offset > current_pos:
            padding_needed = info.offset - current_pos
            data_file.write(b'\0' * padding_needed)
            
        if info.offset is not None:
            data_file.seek(info.offset)
            
        start_offset = data_file.tell()
        data_file.write(tensor.raw_data)
        end_offset = data_file.tell()
        
        # Update external data info
        set_external_data(tensor, info.location, start_offset, end_offset - start_offset)

def _collect_all_tensors(onnx_model_proto):  # type: (ModelProto) -> Iterable[TensorProto]
    """Scan an ONNX model for all tensors and return as an iterator."""
    return chain(_get_initializer_tensors(onnx_model_proto),
                 _get_attribute_tensors(onnx_model_proto))

def _get_initializer_tensors(onnx_model_proto):  # type: (ModelProto) -> Iterable[TensorProto]
    """Create an iterator of initializer tensors from ONNX model."""
    for initializer in onnx_model_proto.graph.initializer:
        yield initializer

def _get_attribute_tensors(onnx_model_proto):  # type: (ModelProto) -> Iterable[TensorProto]
    """Create an iterator of tensors from node attributes of an ONNX model."""
    for node in onnx_model_proto.graph.node:
        for attribute in node.attribute:
            if attribute.t:
                yield attribute.t
            for tensor in attribute.tensors:
                yield tensor

def _clean_path(path):  # type: (Text) -> Text
    """Remove path components which would allow traversing up a directory tree from a base path."""
    # Improved path sanitization
    cleaned = path.lstrip('/\\.')
    # Remove any remaining dangerous components
    parts = cleaned.replace('\\', '/').split('/')
    safe_parts = [p for p in parts if p not in ('..', '.', '')]
    return '/'.join(safe_parts)

def _is_valid_filename(filename):  # type: (Text) -> bool
    """Utility to check whether the provided filename is valid."""
    pattern = re.compile(r"^[^<>:;,?\"*|/]+$")
    return bool(pattern.match(filename))

def uses_external_data(tensor):  # type: (TensorProto) -> bool
    """Return true if the tensor stores data in an external location."""
    return hasattr(tensor, 'data_location') and tensor.data_location == TensorProto.EXTERNAL

def remove_external_data_field(tensor, field_key):  # type: (TensorProto, Text) -> None
    """
    Remove a field from a Tensor's external_data key-value store.
    Modifies tensor object in place.
    @params
    tensor: Tensor object from which value will be removed
    field_key: The key of the field to be removed
    """
    indices_to_remove = []
    for i, field in enumerate(tensor.external_data):
        if field.key == field_key:
            indices_to_remove.append(i)
            
    # Remove in reverse order to avoid index shifting issues
    for i in reversed(indices_to_remove):
        del tensor.external_data[i]

def write_external_data_tensors(model, filepath):  # type: (ModelProto, Text) -> ModelProto
    """
    Serializes data for all the tensors which have data location set to TensorProto.External.
    Note: This function also strips basepath information from all tensors' external_data fields.
    @params
    model: Model object which is the source of tensors to serialize.
    filepath: System path to the directory which should be treated as base path for external data.
    @return
    The modified model object.
    """
    for tensor in _collect_all_tensors(model):
        if uses_external_data(tensor):
            save_external_data(tensor, filepath)
            tensor.raw_data = b''
    return model

import logging
from copy import deepcopy
from typing import Callable, Dict, List, Optional, Tuple, Union
import fvcore.nn.weight_init as weight_init
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F
from detectron2.config import configurable
from detectron2.layers import Conv2d, ShapeSpec, get_norm
from detectron2.modeling import SEM_SEG_HEADS_REGISTRY
from ..transformer.transformer_predictor import TransformerPredictor
from .pixel_decoder import build_pixel_decoder

@SEM_SEG_HEADS_REGISTRY.register()
class ModifiedMaskFormerHead(nn.Module):
    _version = 2
    
    def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
        super().__init__()
        # Initialize internal state for version handling
        self._state_dict_version = None
        
    def load_state_dict_custom(self, state_dict, strict=True):
        """Custom loading logic to handle version conversion"""
        metadata = getattr(self, '_metadata', {})
        local_metadata = dict(metadata.get('version', {}))
        version = local_metadata.get('version', None)
        
        if version is None or version < 2:
            converted_state = {}
            logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
            
            for key in list(state_dict.keys()):
                new_key = key
                if "sem_seg_head" in key and not key.startswith("predictor"):
                    new_key = key.replace("pixel_decoder.", "")
                    # Convert old keys to new format
                    if new_key != key:
                        converted_state[new_key] = state_dict[key]
                    else:
                        converted_state[key] = state_dict[key]
                else:
                    converted_state[key] = state_dict[key]
            
            # Replace original state_dict with converted one
            state_dict = converted_state
            
            if any(k != new_k for k, new_k in zip(list(state_dict.keys()), list(converted_state.keys()))):
                logger.warning(
                    f"Weight format of {self.__class__.__name__} has been updated! "
                    "Please update your models. Applying automatic conversion now ..."
                )
        
        return super().load_state_dict(state_dict, strict=strict)
    
    @configurable
    def __init__(
        self,
        input_shape: Dict[str, ShapeSpec],
        *,
        num_classes: int,
        pixel_decoder: nn.Module,
        loss_weight: float = 1.0,
        ignore_value: int = -1,
        transformer_predictor: nn.Module,
        transformer_in_feature: str,
    ):
        """
        Modified implementation of MaskFormer head with adjusted internal organization.
        
        Args:
            input_shape: shapes (channels and stride) of the input features
            num_classes: number of classes to predict
            pixel_decoder: the pixel decoder module
            loss_weight: loss weight
            ignore_value: category id to be ignored during training.
            transformer_predictor: the transformer decoder that makes prediction
            transformer_in_feature: input feature name to the transformer_predictor
        """
        super().__init__()
        
        # Sort input features by stride
        sorted_inputs = sorted(input_shape.items(), key=lambda x: x[1].stride)
        self.feature_names = [k for k, v in sorted_inputs]
        self.strides = [v.stride for k, v in sorted_inputs]
        self.channels = [v.channels for k, v in sorted_inputs]
        
        # Store configuration parameters
        self.ignored_class_id = ignore_value
        self.common_stride = 4
        self.loss_scale = loss_weight
        self.pixel_encoder = pixel_decoder
        self.classifier = transformer_predictor
        self.input_feature_name = transformer_in_feature
        self.class_count = num_classes
        
    @classmethod
    def from_config(cls, cfg, input_shape: Dict[str, ShapeSpec]):
        selected_features = {
            k: v for k, v in input_shape.items() 
            if k in cfg.MODEL.SEM_SEG_HEAD.IN_FEATURES
        }
        
        # Determine transformer input dimension
        if cfg.MODEL.MASK_FORMER.TRANSFORMER_IN_FEATURE == "transformer_encoder":
            transformer_input_dim = cfg.MODEL.SEM_SEG_HEAD.CONVS_DIM
        else:
            transformer_input_dim = input_shape[cfg.MODEL.MASK_FORMER.TRANSFORMER_IN_FEATURE].channels
            
        return {
            "input_shape": selected_features,
            "ignore_value": cfg.MODEL.SEM_SEG_HEAD.IGNORE_VALUE,
            "num_classes": cfg.MODEL.SEM_SEG_HEAD.NUM_CLASSES,
            "pixel_decoder": build_pixel_decoder(cfg, input_shape),
            "loss_weight": cfg.MODEL.SEM_SEG_HEAD.LOSS_WEIGHT,
            "transformer_in_feature": cfg.MODEL.MASK_FORMER.TRANSFORMER_IN_FEATURE,
            "transformer_predictor": TransformerPredictor(
                cfg,
                transformer_input_dim,
                mask_classification=True,
            ),
        }
    
    def forward(self, features):
        return self.compute_predictions(features)
    
    def compute_predictions(self, features):
        # Extract mask features and transformer encoder features
        mask_feats, encoder_feats = self.pixel_encoder.forward_features(features)
        
        if self.input_feature_name == "transformer_encoder":
            assert encoder_feats is not None, \
                "TransformerEncoderPixelDecoder required when using 'transformer_encoder' feature"
            predictions = self.classifier(encoder_feats, mask_feats)
        else:
            predictions = self.classifier(
                features[self.input_feature_name], mask_feats
            )
        return predictions
    
    def extract_mlp_features(self, features):
        # Extract features for MLP processing
        mask_feats, encoder_feats = self.pixel_encoder.forward_features(features)
        
        if self.input_feature_name == "transformer_encoder":
            assert encoder_feats is not None, \
                "TransformerEncoderPixelDecoder required when using 'transformer_encoder' feature"
            mlp_features = self.classifier.extract_mlp_features(encoder_feats, mask_feats)
        else:
            mlp_features = self.classifier.extract_mlp_features(
                features[self.input_feature_name], mask_feats
            )
            
        return mlp_features

import time
from grpc.framework.base import _interfaces
from grpc.framework.base import interfaces
from grpc.framework.foundation import later

class _TimeoutController(_interfaces.ExpirationManager):
    """A variant implementation of _interfaces.ExpirationManager with adjusted logic."""
    
    def __init__(
        self, operation_lock, termination_ctl, transmission_ctl, ingestion_ctl,
        start_time, requested_timeout, upper_bound_timeout):
        """Constructor.
        Args:
          operation_lock: The operation-wide lock.
          termination_ctl: The _interfaces.TerminationManager for the operation.
          transmission_ctl: The _interfaces.TransmissionManager for the operation.
          ingestion_ctl: The _interfaces.IngestionManager for the operation.
          start_time: The timestamp (seconds since epoch) marking when the operation started.
          requested_timeout: Duration in seconds allowed for the operation.
          upper_bound_timeout: Hard limit on timeout regardless of requests.
        """
        self._lock = operation_lock
        self._termination_ctl = termination_ctl
        self._transmission_ctl = transmission_ctl
        self._ingestion_ctl = ingestion_ctl
        self._start_time = start_time
        self._upper_bound_timeout = upper_bound_timeout
        self._requested_timeout = requested_timeout
        self._end_time = start_time + requested_timeout
        self._sequence_number = 0
        self._scheduled_task = None

    def _handle_expiry(self, seq_num):
        with self._lock:
            if self._scheduled_task is not None and seq_num == self._sequence_number:
                self._scheduled_task = None
                self._termination_ctl.abort(interfaces.Outcome.EXPIRED)
                self._transmission_ctl.abort(interfaces.Outcome.EXPIRED)
                self._ingestion_ctl.abort()

    def begin(self):
        self._sequence_number = 1
        self._scheduled_task = later.later(
            self._requested_timeout, lambda: self._handle_expiry(1))

    def update_timeout(self, new_timeout):
        if self._scheduled_task is not None and new_timeout != self._requested_timeout:
            self._scheduled_task.cancel()
            effective_timeout = min(new_timeout, self._upper_bound_timeout)
            next_sequence = self._sequence_number + 1
            self._requested_timeout = effective_timeout
            self._end_time = self._start_time + effective_timeout
            self._sequence_number = next_sequence
            remaining_delay = max(0.0, self._end_time - time.time())
            self._scheduled_task = later.later(
                remaining_delay, lambda: self._handle_expiry(next_sequence))

    def get_deadline(self):
        return self._end_time

    def terminate_early(self):
        if self._scheduled_task:
            self._scheduled_task.cancel()
            self._scheduled_task = None
        self._sequence_number = None

def create_front_timeout_manager(
    operation_lock, termination_ctl, transmission_ctl, ingestion_ctl,
    timeout):
    """Constructs an ExpirationManager for frontend usage.
    Args:
      operation_lock: The operation-wide lock.
      termination_ctl: The _interfaces.TerminationManager for the operation.
      transmission_ctl: The _interfaces.TransmissionManager for the operation.
      ingestion_ctl: The _interfaces.IngestionManager for the operation.
      timeout: Allowed duration in seconds for the operation.
    Returns:
      An _interfaces.ExpirationManager suitable for frontend use.
    """
    start_timestamp = time.time()
    manager = _TimeoutController(
        operation_lock, termination_ctl, transmission_ctl, ingestion_ctl,
        start_timestamp, timeout, timeout)
    manager.begin()
    return manager

def create_back_timeout_manager(
    operation_lock, termination_ctl, transmission_ctl, ingestion_ctl,
    timeout, fallback_timeout, cap_timeout):
    """Constructs an ExpirationManager for backend usage.
    Args:
      operation_lock: The operation-wide lock.
      termination_ctl: The _interfaces.TerminationManager for the operation.
      transmission_ctl: The _interfaces.TransmissionManager for the operation.
      ingestion_ctl: The _interfaces.IngestionManager for the operation.
      timeout: Requested duration in seconds; may be None to use fallback_timeout.
      fallback_timeout: Default duration when timeout is unspecified.
      cap_timeout: Maximum permissible timeout value.
    Returns:
      An _interfaces.ExpirationManager suitable for backend use.
    """
    start_timestamp = time.time()
    actual_timeout = fallback_timeout if timeout is None else timeout
    manager = _TimeoutController(
        operation_lock, termination_ctl, transmission_ctl, ingestion_ctl,
        start_timestamp, actual_timeout, cap_timeout)
    manager.begin()
    return manager

def setup_logger(log_file_name):
    """
    Ensures the 'logs' directory exists and configures logging to a file.
    
    Args:
        log_file_name: Name of the log file (without path)
        
    Returns:
        tuple: (logging.Logger instance, Path object for the log file)
    """
    logs_dir = Path('logs')
    if not logs_dir.exists():
        logs_dir.mkdir()
    
    log_full_path = logs_dir / log_file_name
    import logging
    logging.basicConfig(
        filename=str(log_full_path),
        format='%(asctime)s %(message)s',
        filemode='w'
    )
    logger = logging.getLogger()
    logger.setLevel(logging.INFO)
    return logger, log_full_path

def deliver_email(content_file, recipients, subject, sender_name) -> str:
    """
    Sends an email with content from a specified file.
    
    Args:
        content_file: Path to the file containing the email body
        recipients: String or list of recipient email addresses
        subject: Subject line for the email
        sender_name: Display name for the sender
        
    Returns:
        Status message indicating success or failure
    """
    sender_addr = '<INSERT_EMAIL_ADDRESS>'
    # Normalize recipients to list if string provided
    if isinstance(recipients, str):
        recipients = [recipients]
    
    with open(content_file) as f:
        content = f.read()
    
    msg = EmailMessage()
    msg.set_content(content)
    msg['From'] = f'{sender_name} <{sender_addr}>'
    msg['To'] = ', '.join(recipients)
    msg['Subject'] = subject
    
    try:
        smtp = smtplib.SMTP('<INSERT_SMTP_RELAY_SERVER_ADDRESS>')
        smtp.send_message(msg)
        smtp.quit()
        return "Successfully sent email"

def fetch_imc_creds(service_name, username):

    Args:
        service_name: Keyring service name
        username: Username associated with the credentials
        
    Returns:
        tuple: (username, password)
    """
    try:

import logging

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
logger_time = logging.getLogger("findy.sql.performance")

# Cache for database engines and sessions
engine_cache = {}
session_cache = {}
indexed_tables = {}

# Event listeners for connection lifecycle management
@event.listens_for(Engine, "connect")
def handle_connection(dbapi_connection, connection_record):
    connection_record.info['process_id'] = os.getpid()

@event.listens_for(Engine, "engine_connect")
def validate_connection(connection, branch):
    if branch:
        return
    
    original_flag = connection.should_close_with_result
    connection.should_close_with_result = False
    
    try:
        connection.scalar(select([1]))
    except exc.DBAPIError as error:
        if getattr(error, 'connection_invalidated', False):
            connection.scalar(select([1]))
        else:
            raise
    finally:
        connection.should_close_with_result = original_flag

@event.listens_for(Engine, "checkout")
def verify_process_identity(dbapi_connection, connection_record, connection_proxy):
    current_pid = os.getpid()
    stored_pid = connection_record.info.get('process_id')
    
    if stored_pid != current_pid:
        connection_record.connection = connection_proxy.connection = None
        raise exc.DisconnectionError(
            f"Connection belongs to process {stored_pid}, "
            f"but requested in process {current_pid}"
        )

@event.listens_for(Engine, "before_cursor_execute")
def log_query_start(conn, cursor, statement, parameters, context, executemany):
    if findy_config['debug'] == 2:
        conn.info.setdefault('query_timestamps', []).append(time.time())
        logger_time.debug(f"Query Started: {statement[:50]}")

@event.listens_for(Engine, "after_cursor_execute")
def log_query_end(conn, cursor, statement, parameters, context, executemany):
    if findy_config['debug'] == 2:
        elapsed = time.time() - conn.info['query_timestamps'].pop()
        logger_time.debug("Query Completed!")
        logger_time.debug(f"Execution Time: {elapsed:.6f} seconds")

@contextlib.contextmanager
def performance_profile():
    profiler = cProfile.Profile()
    profiler.enable()
    try:
        yield
    finally:
        profiler.disable()
        output = StringIO()
        stats = pstats.Stats(profiler, stream=output).sort_stats('cumulative')
        stats.print_stats()
        logger_time.info(output.getvalue())

# Database creation utility
def ensure_database_exists(db_name):
    import psycopg2
    
    # Use environment-specific configuration for connection
    host_key = f'db_host_{findy_config["location"]}'
    port_key = f'db_port_{findy_config["location"]}'
    
    try:
        conn = psycopg2.connect(
            database='postgres',
            user=findy_config['db_user'],
            password=findy_config['db_pass'],
            host=findy_config[host_key],
            port=findy_config[port_key]
        )
        conn.autocommit = True
        
        with conn.cursor() as cursor:
            cursor.execute("SELECT datname FROM pg_database;")
            existing_dbs = [row[0] for row in cursor.fetchall()]
            
            if db_name not in existing_dbs:
                cursor.execute(f"CREATE DATABASE {db_name}")
                logger.info(f"Database '{db_name}' created successfully")
                
    except Exception as err:
        logger.warning(f"Failed to create database '{db_name}': {err}")
        raise
    finally:
        if 'conn' in locals():
            conn.close()

# Engine builder function
def construct_engine(region: Region) -> Engine:
    logger.debug(f"Initializing engine for region: {region}")
    
    db_name = f"{findy_config['db_name']}_{region.value}"
    ensure_database_exists(db_name)
    
    # Build connection string using config values
    host_key = f'db_host_{findy_config["location"]}'
    port_key = f'db_port_{findy_config["location"]}'
    
    connection_uri = (
        f"postgresql+psycopg2://{findy_config['db_user']}:{findy_config['db_pass']}@"
        f"{findy_config[host_key]}:{findy_config[port_key]}/{db_name}"
    )
    
    engine = create_engine(
        connection_uri,
        encoding='utf-8',
        echo=False,
        poolclass=QueuePool,
        pool_size=10,
        pool_recycle=3600,
        max_overflow=2,
        pool_pre_ping=True,
        pool_use_lifo=True,
        executemany_mode='values',
        executemany_values_page_size=10000,
        executemany_batch_page_size=500
    )
    
    logger.debug(f"Successfully connected to {region} database")
    return engine

# Get or create engine with caching
def retrieve_engine(region: Region) -> Engine:
    if region not in engine_cache:
        engine_cache[region] = construct_engine(region)
    return engine_cache[region]

# Index creation logic
def setup_indices(region: Region, engine, base_model):
    if region not in indexed_tables:
        indexed_tables[region] = set()
    
    inspector = Inspector.from_engine(engine)
    
    for table_name, table_obj in base_model.metadata.tables.items():
        if table_name not in indexed_tables[region]:
            indexed_tables[region].add(table_name)
            
            # Get existing indexes for the table
            existing_indexes = [
                idx['name'] for idx in inspector.get_indexes(table_name)
            ]
            
            logger.debug(f"Setting up indices for table '{table_name}' on engine '{engine}'")
            
            # Create single-column indexes
            for column_name in ['timestamp', 'entity_id', 'code', 'report_period', 
                               'created_timestamp', 'updated_timestamp']:
                if column_name in table_obj.c:
                    index_name = f"{table_name}_{column_name}_index"
                    
                    if index_name not in existing_indexes:
                        col_expr = eval(f"table_obj.c.{column_name}")
                        if column_name == 'timestamp':
                            col_expr = eval(f"table_obj.c.{column_name}.desc()")
                        
                        idx = schema.Index(index_name, col_expr)
                        idx.create(engine)
            
            # Create composite indexes
            composite_pairs = [('timestamp', 'entity_id'), ('timestamp', 'code')]
            for col_a, col_b in composite_pairs:
                if col_a in table_obj.c and col_b in table_obj.c:
                    index_name = f"{table_name}_{col_a}_{col_b}_index"
                    
                    if index_name not in existing_indexes:
                        col_a_expr = eval(f"table_obj.c.{col_a}")
                        col_b_expr = eval(f"table_obj.c.{col_b}")
                        
                        idx = schema.Index(index_name, col_a_expr, col_b_expr)
                        idx.create(engine)

# Bind session factory with engine and model
def establish_session(region: Region, provider: Provider, base_model: DeclarativeMeta):
    logger.debug(f"Establishing session for {region}, {provider}, {base_model}")
    
    engine = retrieve_engine(region)
    
    # Ensure tables exist
    base_model.metadata.create_all(engine, checkfirst=True)
    
    # Optional: Create indices (commented out in original)
    # setup_indices(region, engine, base_model)
    
    session_factory = sessionmaker(bind=engine)
    db_session = session_factory()
    
    # Enable batch insert optimization
    enable_batch_inserting(db_session)
    
    return db_session

# Retrieve or create session with caching
def fetch_session(region: Region, provider: Provider, schema_class: object, force_new: bool = False) -> Session:
    db_identifier = get_db_name(data_schema=schema_class)
    session_key = f"{region.value}_{provider.value}_{db_identifier}"
    
    if force_new or session_key not in session_cache:
        session_cache[session_key] = establish_session(region, provider, schema_class)
    
    return session_cache[session_key]

# Compute color centroids for image datasets using K-means clustering

import numpy as np
from pathlib import Path
import argparse
from torchvision.transforms import ToTensor
from sklearn.cluster import KMeans, MiniBatchKMeans
from data import DATASETS

def extract_training_data(dataset_name, data_dir):
    # Load training dataset with automatic download if needed
    train_dataset = DATASETS[dataset_name](
        str(data_dir), train=True, download=True, transform=ToTensor()
    )
    
    # Convert images to numpy arrays and stack them
    images_list = []
    for img, _ in train_dataset:
        images_list.append(img.numpy())
    train_images = np.stack(images_list)
    
    # Reorder dimensions: (N, C, H, W) -> (N, H, W, C)
    train_images = train_images.transpose(0, 2, 3, 1)
    return train_images

def compute_color_centroids(images, cluster_count=16, mb_size=1024):
    # Reshape all pixels into a 2D array for clustering
    pixel_values = images.reshape(-1, images.shape[-1])
    
    # Choose appropriate K-means variant based on batch size
    if mb_size > 0:
        clustering_model = MiniBatchKMeans(
            n_clusters=cluster_count, random_state=0, batch_size=mb_size
        ).fit(pixel_values)
    else:
        clustering_model = KMeans(n_clusters=cluster_count, random_state=0).fit(pixel_values)
    
    # Return the computed centroids (cluster centers)
    return clustering_model.cluster_centers_

def main(config):
    # Setup data directory
    data_directory = Path("data")
    data_directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    
    # Extract and process training data
    training_images = extract_training_data(config.dataset, data_directory)
    
    # Compute centroids using selected clustering method
    color_centroids = compute_color_centroids(
        training_images, 
        config.num_clusters, 
        config.batch_size
    )
    
    # Save results to file
    output_file = data_directory / f"{config.dataset}_centroids.npy"
    np.save(output_file, color_centroids)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    argument_parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    argument_parser.add_argument("--dataset", type=str, choices=list(DATASETS.keys()), default="mnist")
    argument_parser.add_argument("--num_clusters", default=16, type=int)
    argument_parser.add_argument(
        "--batch_size",
        default=1024,
        type=int,
        help="mini-batch size for efficient K-means clustering"
    )
    args = argument_parser.parse_args()
    main(args)

# YouTube Recommendation System - DNN-based Matching Model Implementation

import tensorflow as tf
from tensorflow.keras import Model
from typing import Tuple
from handyrec.features import FeatureGroup, EmbdFeatureGroup
from handyrec.layers import DNN, SampledSoftmaxLayer
from handyrec.layers.utils import concat


def YouTubeMatchDNN(
    user_feature_group: FeatureGroup,
    item_feature_group: EmbdFeatureGroup,
    num_sampled: int = 1,
    dnn_hidden_units: Tuple[int] = (64, 32),
    dnn_activation: str = "relu",
    dnn_dropout: float = 0.0,
    dnn_bn: bool = False,
    l2_dnn: float = 0.0,
    seed: int = 2022,
) -> Model:
    """Constructs a DNN-based matching model for YouTube recommendations.
    
    Parameters
    ----------
    user_feature_group : FeatureGroup
        User feature group containing input features.
    item_feature_group : EmbdFeatureGroup
        Item feature group with embedding capabilities.
    num_sampled : int, optional
        Number of negative samples used in sampled softmax loss, by default ``1``.
    dnn_hidden_units : Tuple[int], optional
        Hidden layer sizes for the user DNN, by default ``(64, 32)``.
    dnn_activation : str, optional
        Activation function applied to hidden layers, by default ``"relu"``.
    dnn_dropout : float, optional
        Dropout rate applied between hidden layers, by default ``0.0``.
    dnn_bn : bool, optional
        Whether to apply batch normalization after each hidden layer, by default ``False``.
    l2_dnn : float, optional
        L2 regularization coefficient for DNN weights, by default ``0.0``.
    seed : int, optional
        Random seed for reproducibility, especially for dropout, by default ``2022``.
    
    Notes
    -----
    Internally, the DNN architecture is extended with an output layer matching the item embedding dimension.
    
    Returns
    -------
    Model
        A compiled Keras model implementing the YouTube DNN matching architecture.
        
    Raises
    ------
    ValueError
        If `item_feature_group` is not an instance of `EmbdFeatureGroup`.
        
    References
    ----------
    .. [1] Covington, Paul, <NAME>, and <NAME>. "Deep neural networks for youtube
        recommendations." Proceedings of the 10th ACM conference on recommender systems. 2016.
    """
    # Validate input type
    if not isinstance(item_feature_group, EmbdFeatureGroup):
        raise ValueError(
            "Item feature group must be an instance of `EmbdFeatureGroup`!"
        )
    
    # Extract embeddings from user features
    user_dense_features, user_sparse_features = user_feature_group.embedding_lookup(pool_method="mean")
    
    # Concatenate dense and sparse user representations
    user_input_tensor = concat(user_dense_features, user_sparse_features)
    
    # Get item ID input and full item embeddings
    item_id_input = item_feature_group.id_input
    all_item_embeddings = item_feature_group.get_embd(item_id_input)
    
    # Build user representation through deep network
    user_vector = DNN(
        hidden_units=dnn_hidden_units,
        activation=dnn_activation,
        output_activation="linear",
        l2_reg=l2_dnn,
        use_bn=dnn_bn,
        dropout_rate=dnn_dropout,
        seed=seed,
        name="User_DNN",
    )(user_input_tensor)
    
    # Compute sampled softmax loss
    final_output = SampledSoftmaxLayer(num_sampled=num_sampled)(
        [all_item_embeddings, user_vector, item_id_input]
    )
    
    # Prepare model inputs and outputs
    user_layer_inputs = list(user_feature_group.input_layers.values())
    
    # Compute actual item embedding for external access
    current_item_embedding = tf.nn.embedding_lookup(all_item_embeddings, item_id_input)
    current_item_embedding = tf.squeeze(current_item_embedding, axis=1)
    
    # Construct complete model
    model = Model(
        inputs=user_layer_inputs + [item_id_input],
        outputs=final_output
    )
    
    # Attach additional attributes for easy access during inference/training
    model.user_input = user_layer_inputs
    model.user_embedding = user_vector
    model.item_input = item_id_input
    model.item_embedding = current_item_embedding
    
    return model
