def _create_tf_to_pytorch_mapping(model, config, tf_weights=None):
    """
    Construct a mapping between TensorFlow variable names and PyTorch module parameters.
    """
    mapping = {}
    
    # Determine backbone model
    backbone_module = model.mobilenet_v1 if isinstance(model, MobileNetV1ForImageClassification) else model
    
    # Initial convolution layer mapping
    base_prefix = "MobilenetV1/Conv2d_0/"
    mapping[base_prefix + "weights"] = backbone_module.conv_stem.convolution.weight
    mapping[base_prefix + "BatchNorm/beta"] = backbone_module.conv_stem.normalization.bias
    mapping[base_prefix + "BatchNorm/gamma"] = backbone_module.conv_stem.normalization.weight
    mapping[base_prefix + "BatchNorm/moving_mean"] = backbone_module.conv_stem.normalization.running_mean
    mapping[base_prefix + "BatchNorm/moving_variance"] = backbone_module.conv_stem.normalization.running_var
    
    # Depthwise separable convolutions mapping
    for idx in range(13):
        tf_idx = idx + 1
        pt_idx = idx * 2
        
        # Depthwise convolution
        depthwise_layer = backbone_module.layer[pt_idx]
        dw_prefix = f"MobilenetV1/Conv2d_{tf_idx}_depthwise/"
        mapping[dw_prefix + "depthwise_weights"] = depthwise_layer.convolution.weight
        mapping[dw_prefix + "BatchNorm/beta"] = depthwise_layer.normalization.bias
        mapping[dw_prefix + "BatchNorm/gamma"] = depthwise_layer.normalization.weight
        mapping[dw_prefix + "BatchNorm/moving_mean"] = depthwise_layer.normalization.running_mean
        mapping[dw_prefix + "BatchNorm/moving_variance"] = depthwise_layer.normalization.running_var
        
        # Pointwise convolution
        pointwise_layer = backbone_module.layer[pt_idx + 1]
        pw_prefix = f"MobilenetV1/Conv2d_{tf_idx}_pointwise/"
        mapping[pw_prefix + "weights"] = pointwise_layer.convolution.weight
        mapping[pw_prefix + "BatchNorm/beta"] = pointwise_layer.normalization.bias
        mapping[pw_prefix + "BatchNorm/gamma"] = pointwise_layer.normalization.weight
        mapping[pw_prefix + "BatchNorm/moving_mean"] = pointwise_layer.normalization.running_mean
        mapping[pw_prefix + "BatchNorm/moving_variance"] = pointwise_layer.normalization.running_var
    
    # Classification head mapping (if applicable)
    if isinstance(model, MobileNetV1ForImageClassification):
        logits_prefix = "MobilenetV1/Logits/Conv2d_1c_1x1/"
        mapping[logits_prefix + "weights"] = model.classifier.weight
        mapping[logits_prefix + "biases"] = model.classifier.bias
    
    return mapping


def load_tf_weights_into_mobilenet_v1(model, config, tf_checkpoint_path):
    """Load weights from TensorFlow checkpoint into PyTorch model."""
    try:
        import numpy as np
        import tensorflow as tf
    except ImportError:
        logger.error(
            "Loading TensorFlow models requires TensorFlow. See https://www.tensorflow.org/install/"
        )
        raise
    
    # Load TF variables
    tf_vars = tf.train.list_variables(tf_checkpoint_path)
    tf_weight_dict = {}
    
    for var_name, shape in tf_vars:
        logger.info(f"Loading TF weight {var_name} with shape {shape}")
        tf_weight_dict[var_name] = tf.train.load_variable(tf_checkpoint_path, var_name)
    
    # Create weight mapping
    weight_map = _create_tf_to_pytorch_mapping(model, config, tf_weight_dict)
    
    # Transfer weights
    for tf_name, pt_module in weight_map.items():
        logger.info(f"Importing {tf_name}")
        
        if tf_name not in tf_weight_dict:
            logger.info(f"{tf_name} not found in TF weights, skipping")
            continue
            
        tf_array = tf_weight_dict[tf_name]
        
        # Handle depthwise convolution transpose
        if "depthwise_weights" in tf_name:
            logger.info("Transposing depthwise weights")
            tf_array = np.transpose(tf_array, (2, 3, 0, 1))
        # Handle regular convolution transpose
        elif "weights" in tf_name:
            logger.info("Transposing weights")
            if len(pt_module.shape) == 2:  # Linear layer
                tf_array = tf_array.squeeze().transpose()
            else:  # Conv layer
                tf_array = np.transpose(tf_array, (3, 2, 0, 1))
        
        # Verify shapes match
        if pt_module.data.shape != tf_array.shape:
            raise ValueError(f"Shape mismatch: {pt_module.data.shape} vs {tf_array.shape}")
        
        # Assign weight
        logger.info(f"Initialize PyTorch weight {tf_name} with shape {tf_array.shape}")
        pt_module.data = torch.from_numpy(tf_array)
        
        # Clean up loaded TF weights
        tf_weight_dict.pop(tf_name, None)
        tf_weight_dict.pop(tf_name + "/RMSProp", None)
        tf_weight_dict.pop(tf_name + "/RMSProp_1", None)
        tf_weight_dict.pop(tf_name + "/ExponentialMovingAverage", None)
    
    # Log remaining weights that weren't used
    unused_weights = list(tf_weight_dict.keys())
    if unused_weights:
        logger.info(f"Unused TF weights: {', '.join(unused_weights)}")
    
    return model


def apply_tf_padding_style(tensor: torch.Tensor, conv_op: nn.Conv2d) -> torch.Tensor:
    """
    Apply TensorFlow-style 'SAME' padding to maintain spatial dimensions during convolution.
    Based on TensorFlow's padding algorithm: https://www.tensorflow.org/api_docs/python/tf/nn#notes_on_padding_2
    """
    batch_size, channels, height, width = tensor.shape
    stride_h, stride_w = conv_op.stride
    kernel_h, kernel_w = conv_op.kernel_size
    
    # Calculate padding along height dimension
    if height % stride_h == 0:
        pad_h = max(kernel_h - stride_h, 0)
    else:
        pad_h = max(kernel_h - (height % stride_h), 0)
    
    # Calculate padding along width dimension
    if width % stride_w == 0:
        pad_w = max(kernel_w - stride_w, 0)
    else:
        pad_w = max(kernel_w - (width % stride_w), 0)
    
    # Split padding between start and end
    pad_left = pad_w // 2
    pad_right = pad_w - pad_left
    pad_top = pad_h // 2
    pad_bottom = pad_h - pad_top
    
    # Apply padding
    return nn.functional.pad(tensor, (pad_left, pad_right, pad_top, pad_bottom), mode="constant", value=0.0)


class MobileNetV1BasicLayer(nn.Module):
    """Basic building block for MobileNetV1: Conv + BatchNorm + Activation"""
    
    def __init__(
        self,
        config: MobileNetV1Config,
        input_filters: int,
        output_filters: int,
        kernel_size: int,
        stride: int = 1,
        groups: int = 1,
        use_bias: bool = False,
        include_batch_norm: bool = True,
        activation_type: Union[bool, str] = True,
    ):
        super().__init__()
        self.config = config
        
        # Validate divisibility constraints
        if input_filters % groups != 0:
            raise ValueError(f"Input filters ({input_filters}) must be divisible by groups ({groups})")
        if output_filters % groups != 0:
            raise ValueError(f"Output filters ({output_filters}) must be divisible by groups ({groups})")
        
        # Set padding based on configuration
        padding = 0 if config.tf_padding else (kernel_size - 1) // 2
        
        # Create convolutional layer
        self.convolution = nn.Conv2d(
            in_channels=input_filters,
            out_channels=output_filters,
            kernel_size=kernel_size,
            stride=stride,
            padding=padding,
            groups=groups,
            bias=use_bias,
            padding_mode="zeros",
        )
        
        # Add batch normalization if requested
        if include_batch_norm:
            self.normalization = nn.BatchNorm2d(
                num_features=output_filters,
                eps=config.layer_norm_eps,
                momentum=0.9997,
                affine=True,
                track_running_stats=True,
            )
        else:
            self.normalization = None
            
        # Set activation function
        if activation_type is not None:
            if isinstance(activation_type, str):
                self.activation = ACT2FN[activation_type]
            elif isinstance(config.hidden_act, str):
                self.activation = ACT2FN[config.hidden_act]
            else:
                self.activation = config.hidden_act
        else:
            self.activation = None
    
    def forward(self, features: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        # Apply TensorFlow-style padding if enabled
        if self.config.tf_padding:
            features = apply_tf_padding_style(features, self.convolution)
        
        # Apply convolution
        features = self.convolution(features)
        
        # Apply batch normalization if present
        if self.normalization is not None:
            features = self.normalization(features)
        
        # Apply activation function if present
        if self.activation is not None:
            features = self.activation(features)
            
        return features


class MobileNetV1BaseModel(PreTrainedModel):
    """Abstract class handling weight initialization and model loading."""
    
    config_class = MobileNetV1Config
    load_tf_weights = load_tf_weights_into_mobilenet_v1
    base_model_prefix = "mobilenet_v1"
    main_input_name = "pixel_values"
    supports_gradient_checkpointing = False
    _no_split_modules = []
    
    def _initialize_weights(self, module: Union[nn.Linear, nn.Conv2d, nn.BatchNorm2d]) -> None:
        """Weight initialization strategy."""
        if isinstance(module, (nn.Linear, nn.Conv2d)):
            module.weight.data.normal_(mean=0.0, std=self.config.initializer_range)
            if module.bias is not None:
                module.bias.data.zero_()
        elif isinstance(module, nn.BatchNorm2d):
            module.bias.data.zero_()
            module.weight.data.fill_(1.0)

@add_start_docstrings(
    "The bare MobileNetV1 model outputting raw hidden-states without any specific head on top.",
    MOBILENET_V1_BASE_DOCSTRING,
)
class MobileNetV1Core(MobileNetV1BaseModel):
    """Core MobileNetV1 architecture without classification head."""
    
    def __init__(self, config: MobileNetV1Config, include_pooling: bool = True):
        super().__init__(config)
        self.config = config
        
        # Initial filter count
        initial_depth = 32
        current_channels = max(int(initial_depth * config.depth_multiplier), config.min_depth)
        
        # First convolution layer
        self.stem_conv = MobileNetV1BasicLayer(
            config,
            input_filters=config.num_channels,
            output_filters=current_channels,
            kernel_size=3,
            stride=2,
        )
        
        # Define layer strides
        layer_strides = [1, 2, 1, 2, 1, 2, 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, 2, 1]
        
        # Build main layers
        self.layers = nn.ModuleList()
        for i in range(13):
            prev_channels = current_channels
            
            # Update channel count when needed
            if layer_strides[i] == 2 or i == 0:
                initial_depth *= 2
                current_channels = max(int(initial_depth * config.depth_multiplier), config.min_depth)
            
            # Depthwise convolution
            self.layers.append(
                MobileNetV1BasicLayer(
                    config,
                    input_filters=prev_channels,
                    output_filters=prev_channels,
                    kernel_size=3,
                    stride=layer_strides[i],
                    groups=prev_channels,
                )
            )
            
            # Pointwise convolution
            self.layers.append(
                MobileNetV1BasicLayer(
                    config,
                    input_filters=prev_channels,
                    output_filters=current_channels,
                    kernel_size=1,
                )
            )
        
        # Pooling layer
        self.pooling = nn.AdaptiveAvgPool2d((1, 1)) if include_pooling else None
        
        # Initialize weights
        self._post_initialization()
    
    def _prune_heads(self, heads_to_prune):
        raise NotImplementedError("Pruning heads not supported for this model.")
    
    @add_start_docstrings_to_model_forward(MOBILENET_V1_INPUTS_DOCSTRING)
    @add_code_sample_docstrings(
        checkpoint=_CHECKPOINT_FOR_DOC,
        output_type=BaseModelOutputWithPoolingAndNoAttention,
        config_class=_CONFIG_FOR_DOC,
        modality="vision",
        expected_output=_EXPECTED_OUTPUT_SHAPE,
    )
    def forward(
        self,
        pixel_values: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
        output_hidden_states: Optional[bool] = None,
        return_dict: Optional[bool] = None,
    ) -> Union[tuple, BaseModelOutputWithPoolingAndNoAttention]:
        # Process arguments
        output_hidden_states = (
            output_hidden_states if output_hidden_states is not None else self.config.output_hidden_states
        )
        return_dict = return_dict if return_dict is not None else self.config.use_return_dict
        
        # Validate inputs
        if pixel_values is None:
            raise ValueError("Input tensor 'pixel_values' must be provided")
        
        # Process through network
        hidden_states = self.stem_conv(pixel_values)
        all_hidden_states = () if output_hidden_states else None
        
        for layer_idx, layer_module in enumerate(self.layers):
            hidden_states = layer_module(hidden_states)
            if output_hidden_states:
                all_hidden_states += (hidden_states,)
        
        last_hidden_state = hidden_states
        
        # Apply pooling if configured
        if self.pooling is not None:
            pooled = torch.flatten(self.pooling(last_hidden_state), start_dim=1)
        else:
            pooled = None
        
        # Return outputs
        if not return_dict:
            return tuple(x for x in [last_hidden_state, pooled, all_hidden_states] if x is not None)
        
        return BaseModelOutputWithPoolingAndNoAttention(
            last_hidden_state=last_hidden_state,
            pooler_output=pooled,
            hidden_states=all_hidden_states,
        )


@add_start_docstrings(
    """
    MobileNetV1 model with an image classification head on top (a linear layer on top of the pooled features).
    """,
    MOBILENET_V1_BASE_DOCSTRING,
)
class MobileNetV1ForImageClassification(MobileNetV1BaseModel):
    """MobileNetV1 with classification head for image classification tasks."""
    
    def __init__(self, config: MobileNetV1Config) -> None:
        super().__init__(config)
        self.num_labels = config.num_labels
        
        # Base model
        self.backbone = MobileNetV1Core(config)
        
        # Get last layer's output size
        last_layer_size = self.backbone.layers[-1].convolution.out_channels
        
        # Classification head
        self.dropout = nn.Dropout(config.classifier_dropout_prob, inplace=True)
        self.classifier = nn.Linear(last_layer_size, config.num_labels) if config.num_labels > 0 else nn.Identity()
        
        # Initialize weights
        self._post_initialization()
    
    @add_start_docstrings_to_model_forward(MOBILENET_V1_INPUTS_DOCSTRING)
    @add_code_sample_docstrings(
        checkpoint=_IMAGE_CLASS_CHECKPOINT,
        output_type=ImageClassifierOutputWithNoAttention,
        config_class=_CONFIG_FOR_DOC,
        expected_output=_IMAGE_CLASS_EXPECTED_OUTPUT,
    )
    def forward(
        self,
        pixel_values: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
        output_hidden_states: Optional[bool] = None,
        labels: Optional[torch.Tensor] = None,
        return_dict: Optional[bool] = None,
    ) -> Union[tuple, ImageClassifierOutputWithNoAttention]:
        """
        Forward pass for image classification.
        
        Args:
            pixel_values: Input images
            output_hidden_states: Whether to return hidden states
            labels: Ground truth labels
            return_dict: Whether to return dict output
            
        Returns:
            Loss and/or predictions depending on inputs
        """
        # Process arguments
        return_dict = return_dict if return_dict is not None else self.config.use_return_dict
        
        # Extract features
        outputs = self.backbone(
            pixel_values, 
            output_hidden_states=output_hidden_states, 
            return_dict=return_dict
        )
        
        # Get pooled features
        pooled_features = outputs.pooler_output if return_dict else outputs[1]
        
        # Apply classifier
        logits = self.classifier(self.dropout(pooled_features))
        
        # Compute loss if labels provided
        loss = None
        if labels is not None:
            if self.config.problem_type is None:
                if self.num_labels == 1:
                    self.config.problem_type = "regression"
                elif self.num_labels > 1 and labels.dtype in (torch.long, torch.int):
                    self.config.problem_type = "single_label_classification"
                else:
                    self.config.problem_type = "multi_label_classification"
            
            if self.config.problem_type == "regression":
                loss_fn = MSELoss()
                if self.num_labels == 1:
                    loss = loss_fn(logits.squeeze(), labels.squeeze())
                else:
                    loss = loss_fn(logits, labels)
            elif self.config.problem_type == "single_label_classification":
                loss_fn = CrossEntropyLoss()
                loss = loss_fn(logits.view(-1, self.num_labels), labels.view(-1))
            elif self.config.problem_type == "multi_label_classification":
                loss_fn = BCEWithLogitsLoss()
                loss = loss_fn(logits, labels)
        
        # Prepare output
        if not return_dict:
            output = (logits,) + (outputs.hidden_states if return_dict else outputs[2:])
            return ((loss,) + output) if loss is not None else output
        
        return ImageClassifierOutputWithNoAttention(
            loss=loss,
            logits=logits,
            hidden_states=outputs.hidden_states,
        )

# PowerPoint automation utility using win32com for reading, editing, and exporting presentations

import os
import argparse
from pathlib import Path

# Application identifiers mapping
APP_IDS = {
    "powerpoint": ["PowerPoint.Application"],
    "wps": ["KWPP.Application", "WPP.Application"],
}

# Constants for PowerPoint operations
EXPORT_FORMAT_PDF = 32
SLIDE_LAYOUT_TITLE_ONLY = 1

def launch_application(app_name: str, show_window: bool):
    """Attempt to start the specified presentation application with fallback."""
    import win32com.client  # type: ignore
    
    app_ids = APP_IDS.get(app_name, [])
    for identifier in app_ids:
        try:
            app = win32com.client.Dispatch(identifier)
            try:
                app.Visible = show_window
            except Exception:
                pass
            return app
        except Exception:
            continue
    
    # Fallback to default PowerPoint if specified app fails
    app = win32com.client.Dispatch("PowerPoint.Application")
    try:
        app.Visible = show_window
    except Exception:
        pass
    return app

def load_presentation(app, file_path: str, show_window: bool):
    """Open a PowerPoint file with error handling."""
    abs_path = os.path.abspath(file_path)
    try:
        return app.Presentations.Open(abs_path, False, False, show_window)
    except Exception:
        return app.Presentations.Open(abs_path)

def save_document(pres, output_file: str, format_type=None):
    """Save presentation with optional format specification."""
    if format_type is None:
        pres.SaveAs(output_file)
    else:
        pres.SaveAs(output_file, format_type)

def extract_text_from_shapes(shapes):
    """Generator yielding text content from shapes that contain text frames."""
    for shape in shapes:
        try:
            if hasattr(shape, 'HasTextFrame') and shape.HasTextFrame and hasattr(shape.TextFrame, 'HasText') and shape.TextFrame.HasText:
                yield shape.TextFrame.TextRange.Text
        except Exception:
            continue

def cmd_read_content(args):
    """Extract main slide text content."""
    app = launch_application(args.app, args.visible)
    pres = load_presentation(app, args.input, args.visible)
    lines = []
    
    for idx, slide in enumerate(pres.Slides, start=1):
        lines.append(f"# Slide {idx}")
        for text in extract_text_from_shapes(slide.Shapes):
            if text.strip():
                lines.append(text.strip())
    
    content = "\n".join(lines)
    if args.output:
        Path(args.output).write_text(content, encoding="utf-8")
    else:
        print(content)
    
    pres.Close()
    app.Quit()

def cmd_read_notes(args):
    """Extract speaker notes from slides."""
    app = launch_application(args.app, args.visible)
    pres = load_presentation(app, args.input, args.visible)
    lines = []
    
    for idx, slide in enumerate(pres.Slides, start=1):
        lines.append(f"# Slide {idx} Notes")
        try:
            notes_shapes = slide.NotesPage.Shapes
            for text in extract_text_from_shapes(notes_shapes):
                if text.strip():
                    lines.append(text.strip())
        except Exception:
            pass
    
    content = "\n".join(lines)
    if args.output:
        Path(args.output).write_text(content, encoding="utf-8")
    else:
        print(content)
    
    pres.Close()
    app.Quit()

def cmd_extract_outline(args):
    """Extract slide titles as an outline structure."""
    app = launch_application(args.app, args.visible)
    pres = load_presentation(app, args.input, args.visible)
    lines = []
    
    for idx, slide in enumerate(pres.Slides, start=1):
        title = ""
        try:
            if hasattr(slide.Shapes, 'HasTitle') and slide.Shapes.HasTitle:
                title_obj = slide.Shapes.Title
                if hasattr(title_obj, 'TextFrame') and hasattr(title_obj.TextFrame, 'TextRange'):
                    title = title_obj.TextFrame.TextRange.Text.strip()
        except Exception:
            pass
        lines.append(f"{idx}. {title}")
    
    content = "\n".join(lines)
    if args.output:
        Path(args.output).write_text(content, encoding="utf-8")
    else:
        print(content)
    
    pres.Close()
    app.Quit()

def cmd_export_content(args):
    """Export presentation to PDF or image files."""
    app = launch_application(args.app, args.visible)
    pres = load_presentation(app, args.input, args.visible)
    
    if args.format == "pdf":
        save_document(pres, args.output, EXPORT_FORMAT_PDF)
    else:
        out_dir = Path(args.outdir)
        out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        pres.Export(str(out_dir), "PNG")
    
    pres.Close()
    app.Quit()

def cmd_replace_text(args):
    """Find and replace text across all slides."""
    app = launch_application(args.app, args.visible)
    pres = load_presentation(app, args.input, args.visible)
    
    for slide in pres.Slides:
        for shape in slide.Shapes:
            try:
                if hasattr(shape, 'HasTextFrame') and shape.HasTextFrame and hasattr(shape.TextFrame, 'HasText') and shape.TextFrame.HasText:
                    text_range = shape.TextFrame.TextRange
                    text_range.Text = text_range.Text.replace(args.find, args.replace)
            except Exception:
                continue
    
    save_document(pres, args.save)
    pres.Close()
    app.Quit()

def cmd_add_slide(args):
    """Insert a new slide at specified index."""
    app = launch_application(args.app, args.visible)
    pres = load_presentation(app, args.input, args.visible)
    
    pres.Slides.Add(args.index, SLIDE_LAYOUT_TITLE_ONLY)
    save_document(pres, args.save)
    
    pres.Close()
    app.Quit()

def cmd_remove_slide(args):
    """Delete a specific slide by index."""
    app = launch_application(args.app, args.visible)
    pres = load_presentation(app, args.input, args.visible)
    
    pres.Slides(args.index).Delete()
    save_document(pres, args.save)
    
    pres.Close()
    app.Quit()

def cmd_modify_font(args):
    """Change font properties of text in slides."""
    app = launch_application(args.app, args.visible)
    pres = load_presentation(app, args.input, args.visible)
    
    for slide in pres.Slides:
        for shape in slide.Shapes:
            try:
                if hasattr(shape, 'HasTextFrame') and shape.HasTextFrame and hasattr(shape.TextFrame, 'HasText') and shape.TextFrame.HasText:
                    text_range = shape.TextFrame.TextRange
                    if hasattr(args, 'name') and args.name:
                        text_range.Font.Name = args.name
                    if hasattr(args, 'size') and args.size:
                        text_range.Font.Size = args.size
            except Exception:
                continue
    
    save_document(pres, args.save)
    pres.Close()
    app.Quit()

def cmd_apply_theme(args):
    """Apply a theme to the entire presentation."""
    app = launch_application(args.app, args.visible)
    pres = load_presentation(app, args.input, args.visible)
    
    pres.ApplyTheme(args.theme)
    save_document(pres, args.save)
    
    pres.Close()
    app.Quit()

def cmd_extract_images(args):
    """Export images embedded in the presentation."""
    app = launch_application(args.app, args.visible)
    pres = load_presentation(app, args.input, args.visible)
    
    out_dir = Path(args.outdir)
    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    
    counter = 1
    for slide in pres.Slides:
        for shape in slide.Shapes:
            try:
                # Check for picture types (11=linked picture, 13=picture)
                if hasattr(shape, 'Type') and shape.Type in (11, 13):
                    output_file = out_dir / f"img_{counter}.png"
                    shape.Export(str(output_file), 2)
                    counter += 1
            except Exception:
                continue
    
    pres.Close()
    app.Quit()

from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Iterable, List, Tuple
import numpy as np
import xarray as xr
from omegaconf import OmegaConf
from weathergen.evaluate.export.cf_utils import CfParser
from weathergen.evaluate.export.reshape import Regridder, find_pl
import logging

_logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
_logger.setLevel(logging.INFO)


class NetcdfParser(CfParser):
    """
    Child class for handling NetCDF output format.
    """
    def __init__(self, config: OmegaConf, **kwargs):
        # Assign additional attributes dynamically
        for key, value in kwargs.items():
            setattr(self, key, value)
        
        super().__init__(config=config, grid_type=getattr(self, 'grid_type', 'regular'))
        self.var_mappings = config.get("variables", {})
    
    def process_sample(
        self,
        forecast_step_results: Iterable[Any],
        reference_time: np.datetime64,
    ) -> None:
        """
        Process results from get_data_worker: reshape, concatenate, add metadata, and save.
        """
        processed_arrays = []
        for item in forecast_step_results:
            if item is None:
                continue
            da = item.as_xarray().squeeze()
            filtered_da = da.sel(channel=self.channels)
            reshaped = self.restructure_data(filtered_da)
            processed_arrays.append(reshaped)

        _logger.info(f"Retrieved {len(processed_arrays)} forecast steps for type {self.data_type}.")
        _logger.info(f"Saved sample data to {self.output_format} in {self.output_dir}.")

        if not processed_arrays:
            return

        combined_ds = self.merge_forecast_steps(processed_arrays)
        combined_ds = self.attach_reference_time(combined_ds, reference_time)
        combined_ds = self.apply_attributes(combined_ds)
        combined_ds = self.insert_metadata(combined_ds)
        combined_ds = self.set_encoding(combined_ds)
        combined_ds = self.apply_regridding(combined_ds)
        self.write_to_disk(combined_ds, reference_time)

    def generate_output_path(self, ref_time: np.datetime64) -> Path:
        """Generate output filename based on prefix, run_id, sample index, output directory, format and forecast_ref_time."""
        formatted_frt = np.datetime_as_string(ref_time, unit="h")
        fname = (
            Path(self.output_dir) / 
            f"{self.data_type}_{formatted_frt}_{self.run_id}.{self.file_extension}"
        )
        return fname

    def restructure_data(self, input_array: xr.DataArray) -> xr.Dataset:
        """
        Reshape dataset while preserving grid structure (regular or Gaussian).
        """
        channel_list = input_array.channel.values
        var_map, pressure_levels = find_pl(channel_list)
        data_vars_dict = {}

        for new_var, old_channels in var_map.items():
            if len(old_channels) > 1:
                vals = input_array.sel(channel=old_channels).values
                dims = ["ipoint", "pressure_level"]
            else:
                vals = input_array.sel(channel=old_channels[0]).values
                dims = ["ipoint"]

            data_vars_dict[new_var] = xr.DataArray(vals, dims=dims)

        result_ds = xr.Dataset(data_vars_dict)
        result_ds = result_ds.assign_coords(
            ipoint=input_array.coords["ipoint"],
            pressure_level=pressure_levels,
        )

        if getattr(self, 'grid_type', 'regular') == 'regular':
            # Regular grid path
            indexed = result_ds.set_index(ipoint=("valid_time", "lat", "lon"))
            result_ds = indexed.unstack("ipoint")
        else:
            # Gaussian/unstructured grid path
            indexed2 = result_ds.set_index(ipoint2=("ipoint", "valid_time"))
            unstacked = indexed2.unstack("ipoint2")
            result_ds = unstacked.rename_dims({"ipoint": "ncells"}).rename_vars({"ipoint": "ncells"})

        return result_ds

    def merge_forecast_steps(
        self,
        arrays: List[xr.DataArray],
        dim_name="valid_time",
        var_mode="minimal",
        coord_mode="different",
        compat_mode="equals",
        attr_mode="drop",
        sort_key="valid_time"
    ) -> xr.Dataset:
        """Concatenate multiple DataArrays into one Dataset along time dimension."""
        merged = xr.concat(
            arrays,
            dim=dim_name,
            data_vars=var_mode,
            coords=coord_mode,
            compat=compat_mode,
            combine_attrs=attr_mode,
        ).sortby(sort_key)
        return merged.to_dataset()

    def attach_reference_time(self, dataset: xr.Dataset, ref_time: np.datetime64) -> xr.Dataset:
        """Assign forecast reference time coordinate to the dataset."""
        dataset = dataset.assign_coords(forecast_reference_time=ref_time)
        if "sample" in dataset.coords:
            dataset = dataset.drop_vars("sample")
        step_hours = self.fstep_hours.astype("int64")
        dataset["forecast_step"] = dataset["forecast_step"] * step_hours
        return dataset

    def apply_attributes(self, dataset: xr.Dataset) -> xr.Dataset:
        """Add CF-compliant attributes to variables depending on grid type."""
        if getattr(self, 'grid_type', '') == 'gaussian':
            var_attrs = self._build_gaussian_attrs(dataset)
        else:
            var_attrs = self._build_regular_attrs(dataset)

        merged_ds = xr.merge([v for v in var_attrs.values()])
        merged_ds.attrs.update(dataset.attrs)
        return merged_ds

    def insert_metadata(self, dataset: xr.Dataset) -> xr.Dataset:
        """Add top-level CF conventions and project info."""
        dataset.attrs.update({
            "title": f"WeatherGenerator Output for {self.run_id} using stream {self.stream}",
            "institution": "WeatherGenerator Project",
            "source": "WeatherGenerator v0.0",
            "history": "Created using the export_inference.py script on " + np.datetime_as_string(np.datetime64("now"), unit="s"),
            "Conventions": "CF-1.12"
        })
        if "stream" in dataset.coords:
            dataset = dataset.drop_vars("stream")
        return dataset

    def set_encoding(self, dataset: xr.Dataset) -> xr.Dataset:
        """Apply time encoding and auxiliary coordinate settings."""
        time_units = {"units": "hours since 1970-01-01 00:00:00", "calendar": "gregorian"}
        if "valid_time" in dataset.coords:
            dataset["valid_time"].encoding.update(time_units)
        if "forecast_reference_time" in dataset.coords:
            dataset["forecast_reference_time"].encoding.update(time_units)
        if "forecast_period" in dataset.coords:
            dataset["forecast_period"].encoding["coordinates"] = "forecast_reference_time"
        return dataset

    def _build_gaussian_attrs(self, ds: xr.Dataset) -> dict:
        """Build CF-compliant attributes for Gaussian grids."""
        dim_config = self.config.get("dimensions", {})
        ds, dim_attrs = self._apply_dim_metadata(ds, dim_config)
        result = {}
        for orig_var, da in ds.data_vars.items():
            mapping = self.var_mappings.get(orig_var, {})
            var_name = mapping.get("var", orig_var)
            std_name = mapping.get("std", orig_var)
            unit = mapping.get("std_unit", "unknown")
            long_name = mapping.get("long", "")
            coord_info = self._construct_coords(ds, mapping, dim_attrs)

            attrs = {
                "standard_name": std_name,
                "units": unit,
            }
            if long_name:
                attrs["long_name"] = long_name

            result[var_name] = xr.DataArray(
                data=da.values,
                dims=da.dims,
                coords=coord_info,
                attrs=attrs,
                name=var_name,
            )
        return result

    def _build_regular_attrs(self, ds: xr.Dataset) -> dict:
        """Build CF-compliant attributes for regular grids."""
        dim_config = self.config.get("dimensions", {})
        ds, dim_attrs = self._apply_dim_metadata(ds, dim_config)
        base_dims = ["pressure", "latitude", "longitude", "valid_time"]
        result = {}

        for orig_var, da in ds.data_vars.items():
            mapping = self.var_mappings.get(orig_var, {})
            var_name = mapping.get("var", orig_var)
            level_type = mapping.get("level_type", "")
            dims = [d for d in base_dims if not (level_type == "sfc" and d == "pressure")]
            coord_info = self._construct_coords(ds, mapping, dim_attrs)
            std_name = mapping.get("std", orig_var)
            unit = mapping.get("std_unit", "unknown")
            long_name = mapping.get("long", "")

            attrs = {
                "standard_name": std_name,
                "units": unit,
            }
            if long_name:
                attrs["long_name"] = long_name

            final_coords = {**coord_info, "valid_time": ds["valid_time"].values}
            result[var_name] = xr.DataArray(
                data=da.values,
                dims=dims,
                coords=final_coords,
                attrs=attrs,
                name=var_name,
            )
            if enc := da.encoding.get("coordinates"):
                result[var_name].encoding["coordinates"] = tuple(
                    enc.replace(" lat ", " latitude ").replace(" lon ", " longitude ")
                )
        return result

    def _apply_dim_metadata(self, ds: xr.Dataset, dim_cfg: dict) -> Tuple[xr.Dataset, dict]:
        """Rename dimensions and collect their metadata."""
        dim_meta = {}
        for dim_name, meta in dim_cfg.items():
            wg_name = meta.get("wg", dim_name)
            if dim_name in ds.dims and dim_name != wg_name:
                ds = ds.rename_dims({dim_name: wg_name})
            dim_meta[wg_name] = {
                "standard_name": meta.get("std", wg_name),
                "units": meta.get("std_unit", ""),
                "long_name": meta.get("long", "")
            }
        return ds, dim_meta

    def _construct_coords(self, ds: xr.Dataset, var_cfg: dict, dim_attrs: dict) -> dict:
        """Create coordinate mapping for a given variable."""
        coords = {}
        coord_map = self.config.get("coordinates", {}).get(var_cfg.get("level_type"), {})
        for src_coord, dest_name in coord_map.items():
            coords[dest_name] = (
                ds.coords[src_coord].dims,
                ds.coords[src_coord].values,
                dim_attrs.get(dest_name, {})
            )
        return coords

    def apply_regridding(self, dataset: xr.Dataset) -> xr.Dataset:
        """Regrid dataset if configured."""
        regrid_type = getattr(self, 'regrid_type', None)
        regrid_deg = getattr(self, 'regrid_degree', None)

        if not regrid_type or not regrid_deg:
            _logger.info("No regridding specified, skipping regridding step.")
            return dataset

        regridder = Regridder(
            dataset,
            output_grid_type=regrid_type,
            degree=regrid_deg
        )
        return regridder.regrid_ds()

    def write_to_disk(self, dataset: xr.Dataset, ref_time: np.datetime64) -> None:
        """Save the dataset to a NetCDF file."""
        output_path = self.generate_output_path(ref_time)
        _logger.info(f"Saving to {output_path}.")
        dataset.to_netcdf(output_path)
        _logger.info(f"Saved NetCDF file to {output_path}.")

# Alembic environment script for database migrations
import os
import logging
from logging.config import fileConfig
from alembic import context
from sqlalchemy import engine_from_config, pool
from any_llm.gateway.db.models import Base

# Initialize logger
logger = logging.getLogger("alembic")

# Load Alembic configuration
config = context.config

# Configure logging based on .ini file settings
if config.config_file_name is not None:
    fileConfig(config.config_file_name)

# Set target metadata for autogenerate support
target_metadata = Base.metadata

# Determine database URL with priority: programmatic -> GATEWAY_DATABASE_URL -> DATABASE_URL -> default
db_url_option = config.get_main_option("sqlalchemy.url")
if db_url_option is None:
    # Try environment variables in order of priority
    database_url = (
        os.getenv("GATEWAY_DATABASE_URL") or 
        os.getenv("DATABASE_URL") or 
        "postgresql://gateway:gateway@localhost:5432/gateway"
    )
    config.set_main_option("sqlalchemy.url", database_url)

def run_migrations_offline_mode() -> None:
    """Execute migrations without establishing a database connection.
    
    Uses direct URL binding instead of an Engine object.
    """
    url = config.get_main_option("sqlalchemy.url")
    context.configure(
        url=url,
        target_metadata=target_metadata,
        literal_binds=True,
        dialect_opts={"paramstyle": "named"},
    )
    with context.begin_transaction():
        context.run_migrations()

def run_migrations_online_mode() -> None:
    """Execute migrations using an active database connection.
    
    Creates an Engine and establishes a connection for migration operations.
    """
    connectable = engine_from_config(
        config.get_section(config.config_ini_section, {}),
        prefix="sqlalchemy.",
        poolclass=pool.NullPool,
    )
    
    with connectable.connect() as conn:
        context.configure(connection=conn, target_metadata=target_metadata)
        with context.begin_transaction():
            context.run_migrations()

# Execute appropriate migration method based on runtime mode
if context.is_offline_mode():
    run_migrations_offline_mode()
else:
    run_migrations_online_mode()

import httpx
import os
import logging
from urllib.parse import urlparse
from fastapi import Request

async def fetch_user_identifier(api_host: str, session_token: str) -> str:
    """
    Fetches the user identifier from the Rancher API using the provided session token.
    """
    endpoint_url = f"{api_host}/v3/users?me=true"
    
    try:
        async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=httpx.Timeout(5.0), verify=False) as client:
            response = await client.get(
                endpoint_url,
                headers={
                    "Cookie": f"R_SESS={session_token}",
                    "Accept": "application/json",
                }
            )
            
            response_data = response.json()
            
            # Validate response structure and status
            is_error_response = (
                response_data.get("type") == "error" or 
                response.status_code != 200 or 
                "data" not in response_data or 
                len(response_data["data"]) == 0
            )
            
            if is_error_response:
                logging.error("User lookup failed: HTTP %d - %s", response.status_code, response_data)
                raise Exception("Unable to retrieve user ID from Rancher API")
            
            user_identifier = response_data["data"][0]["id"]
            
            if user_identifier:
                logging.info("User lookup successful: HTTP %d - userId %s", response.status_code, user_identifier)
                return user_identifier
                
    except Exception as exception:
        logging.error("User API request encountered an error: %s", str(exception))
        
    return None

async def extract_user_id_from_http_request(http_request: Request) -> str:
    """
    Extracts the user ID by retrieving the session token from the HTTP request cookies
    and making a call to the Rancher API.
    """
    rancher_base_url = os.environ.get("RANCHER_URL", "")
    session_cookie_value = http_request.cookies.get("R_SESS")
    
    api_endpoint = ""
    
    if not session_cookie_value:
        logging.warning("Missing R_SESS cookie in request")
        return None
    
    if rancher_base_url:
        parsed_url = urlparse(rancher_base_url)
        protocol = parsed_url.scheme or "https"
        domain = parsed_url.netloc
        api_endpoint = f"{protocol}://{domain}"
    else:
        server_host = http_request.headers.get("Host", "localhost")
        api_endpoint = f"https://{server_host}"
        
    return await fetch_user_identifier(api_endpoint, session_cookie_value)

import asyncio
import sys
from statgpt.cli.commands import create_registry
from statgpt.cli.commands.base import CommandRegistry
from statgpt.cli.repl import run_repl
from statgpt.cli.settings import cli_runtime
from statgpt.cli.shared.console import console, print_error
from statgpt.cli.shared.logging import setup_logging

def _parse_global_options() -> list[str]:
    """Extract and process global CLI flags from command-line arguments.
    
    Returns:
        List of non-flag arguments to be used as commands.
    """
    remaining_args = []
    for item in sys.argv[1:]:
        if item == "--non-interactive":
            cli_runtime.non_interactive = True
        elif item == "--debug":
            cli_runtime.debug = True
        else:
            remaining_args.append(item)
    return remaining_args

async def _run_command(registry: CommandRegistry, argv: list[str]) -> int:
    """Process and execute a single command based on provided arguments.
    
    Returns:
        Exit code: 0 for success, 1 for failure.
    """
    full_cmd = " ".join(argv)
    
    # Handle special built-in commands
    if argv[0] == "help":
        if len(argv) == 1:
            console.print(registry.get_help())
        else:
            target_name = " ".join(argv[1:])
            cmd_obj = registry.get_command(target_name)
            if cmd_obj:
                console.print(cmd_obj.get_help())
            else:
                group_obj = registry.get_group(argv[1])
                if group_obj:
                    console.print(group_obj.get_help())
                else:
                    print_error(f"Unknown command: {target_name}")
                    return 1
        return 0
    
    if argv[0] == "version":
        console.print(f"StatGPT CLI v{registry.version}")
        return 0
    
    try:
        executed = await registry.execute(full_cmd)
        if not executed:
            print_error(f"Unknown command: {argv[0]}")
            console.print("[dim]Run 'statgpt help' for available commands.[/dim]")
            return 1
        return 0
    except Exception as err:
        print_error(f"Command failed: {err}")
        if cli_runtime.debug:
            raise
        return 1

def entrypoint() -> None:
    """Main application entry point for the StatGPT CLI."""
    logger = setup_logging()
    logger.info("StatGPT CLI initialized")
    try:
        reg = create_registry()
        user_args = _parse_global_options()
        
        if user_args:
            exit_status = asyncio.run(_run_command(reg, user_args))
            sys.exit(exit_status)
        else:
            asyncio.run(run_repl(reg))
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        logger.info("CLI execution terminated by user")
        print("\nGoodbye!")
        sys.exit(0)
    except Exception as exc:
        logger.exception("CLI encountered an unexpected error")
        print(f"Error: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        if cli_runtime.debug:
            raise
        sys.exit(1)

# Compute the smallest multiple of y that is >= x

def ceiling_quotient(a: int, b: int) -> int:
    """Compute the ceiling of a divided by b."""
    return (a - 1) // b + 1

def pad_to_multiple(value: int, alignment: int) -> int:
    """Round value up to the nearest multiple of alignment."""
    return ceiling_quotient(value, alignment) * alignment

import os

from esc50_prepare import prepare_esc50
from hyperpyyaml import load_hyperpyyaml
from train_l2i import dataio_prep
import speechbrain as sb
from speechbrain.utils.distributed import run_on_main

class AmortizedNMF(sb.core.Brain):
    """
    SpeechBrain brain class implementing Non-negative Matrix Factorization 
    with learned initialization for audio reconstruction
    """
    
    def forward_pass(self, batch_data, mode=sb.Stage.TRAIN):
        """
        Performs forward computation for NMF-based audio reconstruction
        """
        batch_data = batch_data.to(self.device)
        audio_signals, _ = batch_data.sig
        
        # Compute spectrogram features
        stft_features = self.hparams.compute_stft(audio_signals)
        magnitude_spectrogram = self.hparams.compute_stft_mag(stft_features)
        log_magnitude = torch.log1p(magnitude_spectrogram)
        
        # Encode to latent representation
        latent_codes = self.hparams.nmf_encoder(log_magnitude.permute(0, 2, 1))
        
        # Decode to reconstruct spectrogram
        reconstructed = self.hparams.nmf_decoder(latent_codes)
        
        return reconstructed, audio_signals
    
    def loss_computation(self, model_outputs, original_batch, current_stage=sb.Stage.TRAIN):
        """
        Calculates reconstruction loss using mean squared error on log-spectrograms
        """
        reconstructed, original_audio = model_outputs
        
        # Process target spectrogram
        target_stft = self.hparams.compute_stft(original_audio)
        target_magnitude = self.hparams.compute_stft_mag(target_stft)
        target_log = torch.log1p(target_magnitude).permute(0, 2, 1)
        
        # Compute MSE loss
        reconstruction_error = ((target_log.squeeze() - reconstructed) ** 2).mean()
        
        # Visualization during validation
        with torch.no_grad():
            if (
                self.hparams.epoch_counter.current % self.hparams.checkpoint_interval == 0
                and current_stage == sb.Stage.VALID
            ):
                os.makedirs("reconstructed_specs", exist_ok=True)
                for sample_idx in range(target_stft.shape[0]):
                    output_path = os.path.join("reconstructed_specs", f"{sample_idx}.png")
                    
                    # Plot comparison: ground truth vs reconstruction
                    plt.figure(figsize=(10, 4))
                    plt.subplot(1, 2, 1)
                    plt.imshow(target_log[sample_idx].cpu().numpy(), origin="lower")
                    plt.title("Target")
                    
                    plt.subplot(1, 2, 2)
                    plt.imshow(reconstructed[sample_idx].cpu().numpy(), origin="lower")
                    plt.title("Reconstruction")
                    
                    plt.tight_layout()
                    plt.savefig(output_path)
                    plt.close()
        
        return reconstruction_error
    
    def epoch_ended(self, stage_type, epoch_loss, current_epoch=None):
        """Handles cleanup and logging after each training/validation stage"""
        # Store training statistics
        if stage_type == sb.Stage.TRAIN:
            self.training_loss = epoch_loss
            self.training_metrics = {
                "loss": self.training_loss,
            }
        
        # Handle validation stage
        elif stage_type == sb.Stage.VALID:
            validation_results = {
                "loss": epoch_loss,
            }
            
            # Log metrics and save best model
            if stage_type == sb.Stage.VALID:
                # Record performance statistics
                self.hparams.logger.log_stats(
                    stats_meta={"epoch": current_epoch},
                    train_stats=self.training_metrics,
                    valid_stats=validation_results,
                )
                
                # Save checkpoint based on validation loss
                self.model_saver.save_and_keep_only(
                    meta=validation_results, min_keys=["loss"]
                )

# Speaker identification module based on X-vector architecture
# This implementation uses time-delayed neural networks (TDNN) for feature extraction
# Authors: [redacted]

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import speechbrain as sb
from speechbrain.nnet.CNN import Conv1d
from speechbrain.nnet.linear import Linear
from speechbrain.nnet.normalization import BatchNorm1d
from speechbrain.nnet.pooling import StatisticsPooling

class SpeakerEmbeddingExtractor(torch.nn.Module):
    """Extracts speaker embeddings (x-vectors) for speaker recognition tasks.
    
    This module implements a Time-Delayed Neural Network (TDNN) architecture
    to produce fixed-dimensional speaker embeddings from variable-length input features.
    
    Arguments
    ---------
    device : str
        Device to run the model on ("cpu" or "cuda")
    activation : torch.nn.Module class
        Activation function to use between layers
    tdnn_layers : int
        Number of TDNN layers in the network
    layer_channels : list of ints
        Number of output channels for each TDNN layer
    kernel_sizes : list of ints
        Kernel size for each TDNN layer
    dilations : list of ints
        Dilation factor for each TDNN layer
    embedding_size : int
        Dimensionality of the final embedding vector
    input_features : int
        Number of input feature channels (e.g., 40 for MFCCs)
        
    Example
    -------
    >>> extractor = SpeakerEmbeddingExtractor()
    >>> inputs = torch.randn(5, 10, 40)  # batch_size=5, seq_len=10, features=40
    >>> embeddings = extractor(inputs)
    >>> embeddings.shape  # [batch_size, 1, embedding_dim]
    torch.Size([5, 1, 512])
    """
    
    def __init__(
        self,
        device="cpu",
        activation=torch.nn.LeakyReLU,
        tdnn_layers=5,
        layer_channels=[512, 512, 512, 512, 1500],
        kernel_sizes=[5, 3, 3, 1, 1],
        dilations=[1, 2, 3, 1, 1],
        embedding_size=512,
        input_features=40,
    ):
        super().__init__()
        self.layers = nn.ModuleList()
        
        # Build TDNN layers with convolution, activation, and batch normalization
        current_input_dim = input_features
        for layer_idx in range(tdnn_layers):
            output_dim = layer_channels[layer_idx]
            
            # Add TDNN components: conv layer -> activation -> batch norm
            self.layers.extend([
                Conv1d(
                    in_channels=current_input_dim,
                    out_channels=output_dim,
                    kernel_size=kernel_sizes[layer_idx],
                    dilation=dilations[layer_idx],
                ),
                activation(),
                BatchNorm1d(input_size=output_dim),
            ])
            
            # Update input dimension for next layer
            current_input_dim = output_dim
        
        # Pooling layer to aggregate temporal information
        self.layers.append(StatisticsPooling())
        
        # Final projection to embedding space
        self.layers.append(
            Linear(
                input_size=current_input_dim * 2,  # Concatenated mean and std
                n_neurons=embedding_size,
                bias=True,
                combine_dims=False,
            )
        )
    
    def forward(self, x, lengths=None):
        """Process input features to produce speaker embeddings.
        
        Arguments
        ---------
        x : torch.Tensor
            Input tensor with shape [batch, time, features]
        lengths : torch.Tensor, optional
            Sequence lengths for padding-aware processing
            
        Returns
        -------
        torch.Tensor
            Speaker embeddings with shape [batch, 1, embedding_dim]
        """
        for layer in self.layers:
            try:
                # Some layers accept length parameters
                x = layer(x, lengths=lengths)
            except TypeError:
                # Others don't require additional arguments
                x = layer(x)
        return x


class SpeakerClassifier(sb.nnet.containers.Sequential):
    """Classification head for speaker identification using x-vectors.
    
    This module takes speaker embeddings and produces class probabilities
    for speaker identity prediction.
    
    Arguments
    ---------
    input_shape : tuple
        Expected shape of input embeddings (batch, time, features)
    activation : torch.nn.Module class
        Activation function for hidden layers
    fc_blocks : int
        Number of fully connected blocks
    fc_units : int
        Number of units in fully connected layers
    num_speakers : int
        Number of speakers in classification task
        
    Example
    -------
    >>> input_data = torch.randn(5, 10, 40)
    >>> extractor = SpeakerEmbeddingExtractor()
    >>> embeddings = extractor(input_data)
    >>> classifier = SpeakerClassifier(input_shape=embeddings.shape)
    >>> predictions = classifier(embeddings)
    >>> predictions.shape  # [batch_size, 1, num_speakers]
    torch.Size([5, 1, 1211])
    """
    
    def __init__(
        self,
        input_shape,
        activation=torch.nn.LeakyReLU,
        fc_blocks=1,
        fc_units=512,
        num_speakers=1211,
    ):
        super().__init__(input_shape=input_shape)
        
        # Initial activation and normalization
        self.append(activation(), layer_name="initial_act")
        self.append(sb.nnet.normalization.BatchNorm1d, layer_name="initial_norm")
        
        # Add FC blocks if specified
        if fc_blocks > 0:
            self.append(sb.nnet.containers.Sequential, layer_name="fc_stack")
            
            # Build fully connected layers
            for block_idx in range(fc_blocks):
                block_name = f"block_{block_idx}"
                self.fc_stack.append(
                    sb.nnet.containers.Sequential, 
                    layer_name=block_name
                )
                
                # Linear transformation
                self.fc_stack[block_name].append(
                    sb.nnet.linear.Linear,
                    n_neurons=fc_units,
                    bias=True,
                    layer_name="linear"
                )
                
                # Activation and normalization
                self.fc_stack[block_name].append(
                    activation(), 
                    layer_name="act"
                )
                self.fc_stack[block_name].append(
                    sb.nnet.normalization.BatchNorm1d, 
                    layer_name="norm"
                )
        
        # Output layer for speaker classification
        self.append(
            sb.nnet.linear.Linear, 
            n_neurons=num_speakers, 
            layer_name="output_layer"
        )
        
        # Log-softmax for numerical stability
        self.append(
            sb.nnet.activations.Softmax(apply_log=True), 
            layer_name="log_softmax"
        )

from functools import partial
from metaxy_testing.models import SampleFeatureSpec
from metaxy import BaseFeature, FeatureDep, FeatureKey, FieldKey, FieldSpec
from metaxy.models.field import SpecialFieldDep
from metaxy.models.fields_mapping import AllFieldsMapping, FieldsMapping, FieldsMappingType


def _create_upstream_feature(name: str, field_keys: list):
    """Helper to generate upstream features with specified fields."""
    class_attrs = {
        "__module__": __name__,
        "spec": SampleFeatureSpec(
            key=FeatureKey(["test", name]),
            fields=[FieldSpec(key=FieldKey([k]), code_version="1") for k in field_keys],
        ),
    }
    return type(f"Upstream_{name.title()}", (BaseFeature,), class_attrs)


def _create_downstream_feature_with_all_mapping(
    name: str,
    upstreams: list,
    output_field_key: str,
):
    """Helper to create downstream feature depending on ALL fields from given upstreams."""
    deps = [
        FeatureDep(feature=up, fields_mapping=FieldsMapping.all())
        for up in upstreams
    ]
    spec = SampleFeatureSpec(
        key=FeatureKey(["test", name]),
        deps=deps,
        fields=[
            FieldSpec(
                key=FieldKey([output_field_key]),
                code_version="1",
                deps=SpecialFieldDep.ALL,
            )
        ],
    )
    return type(f"Downstream_{name.title()}", (BaseFeature,), {"spec": spec})


def _assert_field_deps(field, expected_deps):
    assert field.deps == expected_deps, f"Expected {expected_deps}, got {field.deps}"


def test_all_fields_mapping_returns_all():
    """Verify that using FieldsMapping.all() results in SpecialFieldDep.ALL."""
    Upstream = _create_upstream_feature("upstream", ["audio", "video"])
    
    Downstream = _create_downstream_feature_with_all_mapping(
        "downstream", [Upstream], "combined"
    )

    combined_field = Downstream.spec().fields_by_key[FieldKey(["combined"])]
    assert combined_field.deps == SpecialFieldDep.ALL


def test_fields_mapping_all_classmethod():
    """Ensure FieldsMapping.all() yields correct internal structure."""
    Upstream = _create_upstream_feature("upstream", ["audio", "video"])

    Downstream = _create_downstream_feature_with_all_mapping(
        "downstream", [Upstream], "combined"
    )

    combined_field = Downstream.spec().fields_by_key[FieldKey(["combined"])]
    assert combined_field.deps == SpecialFieldDep.ALL

    # Validate internal representation
    mapping_obj = FieldsMapping.all()
    assert isinstance(mapping_obj.mapping, AllFieldsMapping)
    assert mapping_obj.mapping.type == FieldsMappingType.ALL


def test_all_fields_mapping_with_multiple_upstreams():
    """Test aggregation across multiple upstreams via AllFieldsMapping."""
    Up1 = _create_upstream_feature("upstream1", ["audio"])
    Up2 = _create_upstream_feature("upstream2", ["video"])

    Downstream = _create_downstream_feature_with_all_mapping(
        "downstream_multi", [Up1, Up2], "aggregated"
    )

    aggregated_field = Downstream.spec().fields_by_key[FieldKey(["aggregated"])]
    assert aggregated_field.deps == SpecialFieldDep.ALL


def test_all_fields_mapping_serialization():
    """Check serialization/deserialization round-trip for AllFieldsMapping."""
    # Direct instance
    direct_all = AllFieldsMapping()
    serialized_direct = direct_all.model_dump(mode="json")
    assert serialized_direct == {"type": "all"}

    deserialized_direct = FieldsMappingType.ALL.model_validate(serialized_direct)
    assert isinstance(deserialized_direct, AllFieldsMapping)

    # Via FieldsMapping wrapper
    wrapped_all = FieldsMapping.all()
    serialized_wrapped = wrapped_all.model_dump(mode="json")
    assert serialized_wrapped == {"mapping": {"type": "all"}}

    deserialized_wrapped = FieldsMapping.model_validate(serialized_wrapped)
    assert isinstance(deserialized_wrapped.mapping, AllFieldsMapping)


def test_all_fields_mapping_vs_explicit_all():
    """Compare implicit (via mapping) vs explicit SpecialFieldDep.ALL behavior."""
    Upstream = _create_upstream_feature("upstream", ["data"])

    # Implicit via mapping
    class WithMapping(BaseFeature):
        spec = SampleFeatureSpec(
            key=FeatureKey(["test", "with_mapping"]),
            deps=[FeatureDep(feature=Upstream, fields_mapping=FieldsMapping.all())],
            fields=[
                FieldSpec(
                    key=FieldKey(["field1"]),
                    code_version="1",
                )
            ],
        )

    # Explicit dependency
    class WithExplicit(BaseFeature):
        spec = SampleFeatureSpec(
            key=FeatureKey(["test", "with_explicit"]),
            deps=[FeatureDep(feature=Upstream)],
            fields=[
                FieldSpec(
                    key=FieldKey(["field1"]),
                    code_version="1",
                    deps=SpecialFieldDep.ALL,
                )
            ],
        )

    mapping_field = WithMapping.spec().fields_by_key[FieldKey(["field1"])]
    explicit_field = WithExplicit.spec().fields_by_key[FieldKey(["field1"])]

    # At definition time, mapping-based has no explicit deps
    assert mapping_field.deps == []
    assert explicit_field.deps == SpecialFieldDep.ALL

# Test resonator models for port count and frequency behavior

import jax.numpy as jnp
from qpdk.models.resonator import (
    quarter_wave_resonator_coupled,
    resonator,
    resonator_coupled,
    resonator_half_wave,
    resonator_quarter_wave,
)

def test_resonator_models_port_count() -> None:
    freq = jnp.array([5e9])
    
    # Basic resonator and half-wave resonator should each have 2 physical ports (4 S-parameters total)
    base_res = resonator(f=freq, length=2000)
    assert len(base_res) == 4
    
    half_wave_res = resonator_half_wave(f=freq, length=2000)
    assert len(half_wave_res) == 4
    
    # Quarter-wave resonator has 1 physical port; dummy second port is present for layout but 
    # gets removed during circuit evaluation, leaving only 1 S-parameter
    quarter_wave_res = resonator_quarter_wave(f=freq, length=2000)
    assert len(quarter_wave_res) == 1

def test_resonator_coupled_basic_structure() -> None:
    freq = jnp.array([5e9])
    coupled_res = resonator_coupled(f=freq, length=2000)
    # Coupled resonator has 4 ports → 4×4 = 16 S-parameters
    assert len(coupled_res) == 16

def test_resonator_frequency_shifts_with_length() -> None:
    # Use quarter-wave coupled resonator to identify resonance via transmission minima
    # Shorter length → higher resonance frequency
    freq_range = jnp.linspace(2e9, 5e9, 1000)
    
    short_res = quarter_wave_resonator_coupled(f=freq_range, length=8000)
    long_res = quarter_wave_resonator_coupled(f=freq_range, length=10000)
    
    # Extract magnitude of S21 (coupling output to coupling input)
    s21_short_mag = jnp.abs(short_res[("coupling_o2", "coupling_o1")])
    s21_long_mag = jnp.abs(long_res[("coupling_o2", "coupling_o1")])
    
    # Locate resonance frequencies by finding transmission minima
    f_min_short = freq_range[jnp.argmin(s21_short_mag)]
    f_min_long = freq_range[jnp.argmin(s21_long_mag)]
    
    # Longer resonator should resonate at lower frequency
    assert f_min_long < f_min_short

# Fallback encoding for unrecognized models
STANDARD_ENCODING = "cl100k_base"

@lru_cache(maxsize=8)
def _acquire_encoding(encoding_id: str):
    """Retrieve and cache the requested tiktoken encoding."""
    import tiktoken
    return tiktoken.get_encoding(encoding_id)

def determine_encoding_for_model(model_name: str) -> str:
    """Determine the appropriate encoding for a given model name.
    
    Args:
        model_name: The model identifier string (e.g., 'gpt-4o', 'gpt-3.5-turbo').
        
    Returns:
        The corresponding encoding name (e.g., 'o200k_base', 'cl100k_base').
    """
    # First try exact match in mapping
    if model_name in MODEL_ENCODING_MAP:
        return MODEL_ENCODING_MAP[model_name]
    
    # Attempt prefix-based matching for versioned models
    prefixes_to_try = ["gpt-4o", "gpt-4-turbo", "gpt-4", "gpt-3.5", "o1", "o3"]
    for prefix in prefixes_to_try:
        if model_name.startswith(prefix):
            # Find any known model with this prefix
            for known_model, enc in MODEL_ENCODING_MAP.items():
                if known_model.startswith(prefix):
                    return enc
    
    # Default fallback encoding
    return STANDARD_ENCODING

class TiktokenCounter(BaseTokenizer):
    """Token counter leveraging tiktoken for accurate OpenAI model tokenization.
    
    This class provides precise token counting compatible with OpenAI's models,
    including support for chat message formatting overheads and multi-part content.
    
    Example usage:
        counter = TiktokenCounter("gpt-4o")
        tokens = counter.count_text("Hello, world!")
        print(f"Token count: {tokens}")
    """
    
    # Overhead tokens per message in chat completions API
    PER_MESSAGE_OVERHEAD = 3
    # Additional overhead for assistant reply priming
    REPLY_PRIMING_OVERHEAD = 3
    
    def __init__(self, model: str = "gpt-4o"):
        """Initialize the tokenizer with specified model.
        
        Args:
            model: Model identifier to select correct encoding.
                   Defaults to 'gpt-4o' which uses o200k_base encoding.
        """
        self.model_identifier = model
        self.encoding_type = determine_encoding_for_model(model)
        self._cached_encoder = None  # Defer loading until needed
    
    @property
    def tokenizer(self):
        """Lazily load and cache the tokenizer instance."""
        if self._cached_encoder is None:
            self._cached_encoder = _acquire_encoding(self.encoding_type)
        return self._cached_encoder
    
    def count_tokens_in_text(self, text: str) -> int:
        """Count tokens in plain text input.
        
        Args:
            text: Input string to tokenize.
            
        Returns:
            Number of tokens after applying BPE tokenization.
        """
        if not text:
            return 0
        return len(self.tokenizer.encode(text))
    
    def count_chat_messages(self, messages: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> int:
        """Calculate total token count for a list of chat messages.
        
        Implements OpenAI's official token counting rules for chat completions,
        including message structure overhead and special handling for tool calls.
        
        Args:
            messages: List of message dictionaries containing role/content/etc.
            
        Returns:
            Total number of tokens accounting for all message components.
        """
        total_tokens = 0
        
        for msg in messages:
            # Add base overhead per message
            total_tokens += self.PER_MESSAGE_OVERHEAD
            
            for field, value in msg.items():
                if value is None:
                    continue
                    
                if field == "content":
                    if isinstance(value, str):
                        total_tokens += self.count_tokens_in_text(value)
                    elif isinstance(value, list):
                        # Handle multi-part content (text + images)
                        for item in value:
                            if isinstance(item, dict):
                                content_type = item.get("type")
                                if content_type == "text":
                                    total_tokens += self.count_tokens_in_text(item.get("text", ""))
                                elif content_type == "image_url":
                                    detail_level = item.get("image_url", {}).get("detail", "auto")
                                    if detail_level == "low":
                                        total_tokens += 85
                                    else:
                                        total_tokens += 170
                                else:
                                    total_tokens += self.count_tokens_in_text(str(item))
                            elif isinstance(item, str):
                                total_tokens += self.count_tokens_in_text(item)
                                
                elif field == "role":
                    total_tokens += self.count_tokens_in_text(value)
                    
                elif field == "name":
                    total_tokens += self.count_tokens_in_text(value)
                    total_tokens += 1  # Name adds one extra token
                    
                elif field == "tool_calls":
                    for tool in value:
                        total_tokens += 3  # Tool call overhead
                        func_info = tool.get("function", {})
                        total_tokens += self.count_tokens_in_text(func_info.get("name", ""))
                        total_tokens += self.count_tokens_in_text(func_info.get("arguments", ""))
                        if "id" in tool:
                            total_tokens += self.count_tokens_in_text(tool["id"])
                            
                elif field == "tool_call_id":
                    total_tokens += self.count_tokens_in_text(value)
                    
                elif field == "function_call":
                    func_data = value
                    total_tokens += self.count_tokens_in_text(func_data.get("name", ""))
                    total_tokens += self.count_tokens_in_text(func_data.get("arguments", ""))
        
        # Account for assistant priming at end of conversation
        total_tokens += self.REPLY_PRIMING_OVERHEAD
        
        return total_tokens
    
    def convert_to_ids(self, text: str) -> list[int]:
        """Convert text into a sequence of token IDs.
        
        Args:
            text: Input string to encode.
            
        Returns:
            List of integer token IDs.
        """
        return self.tokenizer.encode(text)
    
    def convert_from_ids(self, token_ids: list[int]) -> str:
        """Reconstruct text from token ID sequence.
        
        Args:
            token_ids: List of integer token IDs.
            
        Returns:
            Decoded text string.
        """
        return self.tokenizer.decode(token_ids)
    
    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        return f"TiktokenCounter(model={self.model_identifier!r}, encoding={self.encoding_type!r})"
